facts.title: Your chocolate has a geography.
facts.body: The cocoa in chocolate starts as a tropical crop. Côte d’Ivoire was the largest producer in the 2024 FAO data, growing about 36% of the world total. That makes it a useful place to remember, but a production ranking cannot tell you where a specific brand buys its ingredients.
facts.question: Which country was the largest producer of cocoa beans in 2024?

facts.title: Everest wins one contest. Chimborazo wins another.
facts.body: Ecuador’s Chimborazo has the summit furthest from Earth’s centre. Earth bulges at the equator, giving this volcano an advantage over Everest even though Everest stands higher above sea level.

facts.title: Climate of Albania
facts.body: Mild temperate; cool, cloudy, wet winters; hot, clear, dry summers; interior is cooler and wetter

facts.title: Climate of Angola
facts.body: Semiarid in south and along coast to Luanda; north has cool, dry season (May to October) and hot, rainy season (November to April)

facts.title: Climate of Austria
facts.body: Temperate; continental, cloudy; cold winters with frequent rain and some snow in lowlands and snow in mountains; moderate summers with occasional showers

facts.title: Climate of Australia
facts.body: Generally arid to semiarid; temperate in south and east; tropical in north

facts.title: Climate of Bosnia and Herzegovina
facts.body: Hot summers and cold winters; areas of high elevation have short, cool summers and long, severe winters; mild, rainy winters along coast

facts.title: Climate of Bangladesh
facts.body: Tropical; mild winter (October to March); hot, humid summer (March to June); humid, warm rainy monsoon (June to October)

facts.title: Climate of Burkina Faso
facts.body: Three climate zones including a hot tropical savanna with a short rainy season in the southern half, a tropical hot semi-arid steppe climate typical of the Sahel region in the northern half, and small area of hot desert in the very north of the country bordering the Sahara Desert

facts.title: Climate of Burundi
facts.body: Equatorial; high plateau with considerable altitude variation (772 m to 2,670 m above sea level); average annual temperature varies with altitude from 23 to 17 degrees Celsius but is generally moderate; average annual rainfall is about 150 cm with two wet seasons (February to May and September to November) and two dry seasons (June to August and December to January)

facts.title: Climate of Bhutan
facts.body: Varies; tropical in southern plains; cool winters and hot summers in central valleys; severe winters and cool summers in Himalayas

facts.title: Climate of Belarus
facts.body: Cold winters, cool and moist summers; transitional between continental and maritime

facts.title: Climate of Belize
facts.body: Tropical; very hot and humid; rainy season (May to November); dry season (February to May)

facts.title: Climate of Democratic Republic of the Congo
facts.body: Tropical; hot and humid in equatorial river basin; cooler and drier in southern highlands; cooler and wetter in eastern highlands; north of Equator - wet season (April to October), dry season (December to February); south of Equator - wet season (November to March), dry season (April to October)

facts.title: Climate of Republic of the Congo
facts.body: Tropical; rainy season (March to June); dry season (June to October); persistent high temperatures and humidity; particularly enervating climate astride the Equator

facts.title: Climate of Switzerland
facts.body: Temperate, but varies with altitude; cold, cloudy, rainy/snowy winters; cool to warm, cloudy, humid summers with occasional showers

facts.title: Climate of Côte d’Ivoire
facts.body: Tropical along coast, semiarid in far north; three seasons - warm and dry (November to March), hot and dry (March to May), hot and wet (June to October)

facts.title: Climate of Chile
facts.body: Temperate; desert in north; Mediterranean in central region; cool and damp in south

facts.title: Climate of Cameroon
facts.body: Varies with terrain, from tropical along coast to semiarid and hot in north

facts.title: Climate of Costa Rica
facts.body: Tropical and subtropical; dry season (December to April); rainy season (May to November); cooler in highlands

facts.title: Climate of Cuba
facts.body: Tropical; moderated by trade winds; dry season (November to April); rainy season (May to October)

facts.title: Climate of Germany
facts.body: Temperate and marine; cool, cloudy, wet winters and summers; occasional warm mountain (foehn) wind

facts.title: Climate of Denmark
facts.body: Temperate; humid and overcast; mild, windy winters and cool summers

facts.title: Climate of Dominican Republic
facts.body: Tropical maritime; little seasonal temperature variation; seasonal variation in rainfall

facts.title: Climate of Algeria
facts.body: Arid to semiarid; mild, wet winters with hot, dry summers along coast; drier with cold winters and hot summers on high plateau; sirocco is a hot, dust/sand-laden wind especially common in summer

facts.title: Climate of Ecuador
facts.body: Tropical along coast, becoming cooler inland at higher elevations; tropical in Amazonian jungle lowlands

facts.title: Climate of Eritrea
facts.body: Hot, dry desert strip along Red Sea coast; cooler and wetter in the central highlands (up to 61 cm of rainfall annually, heaviest June to September); semiarid in western hills and lowlands

facts.title: Climate of Spain
facts.body: Temperate; clear, hot summers in interior, more moderate and cloudy along coast; cloudy, cold winters in interior, partly cloudy and cool along coast

facts.title: Climate of Finland
facts.body: Cold temperate; potentially subarctic but comparatively mild because of moderating influence of the North Atlantic Current, Baltic Sea, and more than 60,000 lakes

facts.title: Climate of Micronesia
facts.body: Tropical; heavy year-round rainfall, especially in the eastern islands; located on southern edge of the typhoon belt with occasionally severe damage

facts.title: Climate of France
facts.body: Metropolitan France: generally cool winters and mild summers, but mild winters and hot summers along the Mediterranean; occasional strong, cold, dry, north-to-northwesterly wind known as the mistral

facts.title: Climate of United Kingdom
facts.body: Temperate; moderated by prevailing southwest winds over the North Atlantic Current; more than one-half of the days are overcast

facts.title: Climate of Ghana
facts.body: Tropical; warm and comparatively dry along southeast coast; hot and humid in southwest; hot and dry in north

facts.title: Climate of Gambia
facts.body: Tropical; hot, rainy season (June to November); cooler, dry season (November to May)

facts.title: Climate of Guinea
facts.body: Generally hot and humid; monsoonal-type rainy season (June to November) with southwesterly winds; dry season (December to May) with northeasterly harmattan winds

facts.title: Climate of Guinea-Bissau
facts.body: Tropical; generally hot and humid; monsoonal-type rainy season (June to November) with southwesterly winds; dry season (December to May) with northeasterly harmattan winds

facts.title: Climate of Guyana
facts.body: Tropical; hot, humid, moderated by northeast trade winds; two rainy seasons (May to August, November to January)

facts.title: Climate of Croatia
facts.body: Mediterranean and continental; continental climate predominant with hot summers and cold winters; mild winters, dry summers along coast

facts.title: Climate of Ireland
facts.body: Temperate maritime; modified by North Atlantic Current; mild winters, cool summers; consistently humid; overcast about half the time

facts.title: Climate of Iraq
facts.body: Mostly desert; mild to cool winters with dry, hot, cloudless summers; northern mountainous regions along Iranian and Turkish borders experience cold winters with occasionally heavy snows that melt in early spring, sometimes causing extensive flooding in central and southern Iraq

facts.title: Climate of Iceland
facts.body: Temperate; moderated by North Atlantic Current; mild, windy winters; damp, cool summers

facts.title: Climate of Italy
facts.body: Predominantly Mediterranean; alpine in far north; hot, dry in south

facts.title: Climate of Kyrgyzstan
facts.body: Dry continental to polar in high Tien Shan Mountains; subtropical in southwest (Fergana Valley); temperate in northern foothill zone

facts.title: Climate of Cambodia
facts.body: Tropical; rainy, monsoon season (May to November); dry season (December to April); little seasonal temperature variation

facts.title: Climate of Saint Kitts and Nevis
facts.body: Tropical, tempered by constant sea breezes; little seasonal temperature variation; rainy season (May to November)

facts.title: Climate of North Korea
facts.body: Temperate, with rainfall concentrated in summer; long, bitter winters

facts.title: Climate of South Korea
facts.body: Temperate, with rainfall heavier in summer than winter; cold winters

facts.title: Climate of Laos
facts.body: Tropical monsoon; rainy season (May to November); dry season (December to April)

facts.title: Climate of Lebanon
facts.body: Mediterranean; mild to cool, wet winters with hot, dry summers; the Lebanon Mountains experience heavy winter snows

facts.title: Climate of Saint Lucia
facts.body: Tropical, moderated by northeast trade winds; dry season January to April, rainy season May to August

facts.title: Climate of Liechtenstein
facts.body: Continental; cold, cloudy winters with frequent snow or rain; cool to moderately warm, cloudy, humid summers

facts.title: Climate of Sri Lanka
facts.body: Tropical monsoon; northeast monsoon (December to March); southwest monsoon (June to October)

facts.title: Climate of Liberia
facts.body: Tropical; hot, humid; dry winters with hot days and cool to cold nights; wet, cloudy summers with frequent heavy showers

facts.title: Climate of Lithuania
facts.body: Transitional, between maritime and continental; wet, moderate winters and summers

facts.title: Climate of Morocco
facts.body: Mediterranean in the north, becoming more extreme in the interior; in the south, hot, dry desert; rain is rare; cold offshore air currents produce fog and heavy dew

facts.title: Climate of Montenegro
facts.body: Mediterranean climate, hot dry summers and autumns and relatively cold winters with heavy snowfalls inland

facts.title: Climate of Marshall Islands
facts.body: Tropical; hot and humid; wet season May to November; islands border typhoon belt

facts.title: Climate of North Macedonia
facts.body: Warm, dry summers and autumns; relatively cold winters with heavy snowfall

facts.title: Climate of Mali
facts.body: Subtropical to arid; hot and dry (February to June); rainy, humid, and mild (June to November); cool and dry (November to February)

facts.title: Climate of Myanmar
facts.body: Tropical monsoon; cloudy, rainy, hot, humid summers (southwest monsoon, June to September); less cloudy, scant rainfall, mild temperatures, lower humidity during winter (northeast monsoon, December to April)

facts.title: Climate of Mongolia
facts.body: Desert; continental (large daily and seasonal temperature ranges)

facts.title: Climate of Mauritius
facts.body: Tropical, modified by southeast trade winds; warm, dry winter (May to November); hot, wet, humid summer (November to May)

facts.title: Climate of Maldives
facts.body: Tropical; hot, humid; dry, northeast monsoon (November to March); rainy, southwest monsoon (June to August)

facts.title: Climate of Malawi
facts.body: Sub-tropical; rainy season (November to May); dry season (May to November)

facts.title: Climate of Malaysia
facts.body: Tropical; annual southwest (April to October) and northeast (October to February) monsoons

facts.title: Climate of Norway
facts.body: Temperate along coast, modified by North Atlantic Current; colder interior with increased precipitation and colder summers; rainy year-round on west coast

facts.title: Climate of Nepal
facts.body: Varies from cool summers and severe winters in north to subtropical summers and mild winters in south

facts.title: Climate of Nauru
facts.body: Tropical with a monsoonal pattern; rainy season (November to February)

facts.title: Climate of Oman
facts.body: Dry desert; hot, humid along coast; hot, dry interior; strong southwest summer monsoon (May to September) in far south

facts.title: Climate of Panama
facts.body: Tropical maritime; hot, humid, cloudy; prolonged rainy season (May to January), short dry season (January to May)

facts.title: Climate of Peru
facts.body: Varies from tropical in east to dry desert in west; temperate to frigid in Andes

facts.title: Climate of Papua New Guinea
facts.body: Tropical; northwest monsoon (December to March), southeast monsoon (May to October); slight seasonal temperature variation

facts.title: Climate of Philippines
facts.body: Tropical marine; northeast monsoon (November to April); southwest monsoon (May to October)

facts.title: Climate of Poland
facts.body: Temperate with cold, cloudy, moderately severe winters with frequent precipitation; mild summers with frequent showers and thundershowers

facts.title: Climate of Palestine
facts.body: Temperate; temperature and precipitation vary with altitude, warm to hot summers, cool to mild winters

facts.title: Climate of Portugal
facts.body: Maritime temperate; cool and rainy in north, warmer and drier in south

facts.title: Climate of Paraguay
facts.body: Subtropical to temperate; substantial rainfall in the eastern portions, becoming semiarid in the far west

facts.title: Climate of Romania
facts.body: Temperate; cold, cloudy winters with frequent snow and fog; sunny summers with frequent showers and thunderstorms

facts.title: Climate of Serbia
facts.body: In the north, continental climate (cold winters and hot, humid summers with well-distributed rainfall); in other parts, continental and Mediterranean climate (relatively cold winters with heavy snowfall and hot, dry summers and autumns)

facts.title: Climate of Russia
facts.body: Ranges from steppes in the south through humid continental in much of European Russia; subarctic in Siberia to tundra climate in the polar north; winters vary from cool along Black Sea coast to frigid in Siberia; summers vary from warm in the steppes to cool along Arctic coast

facts.title: Climate of Rwanda
facts.body: Temperate; two rainy seasons (February to April, November to January); mild in mountains with frost and snow possible

facts.title: Climate of Seychelles
facts.body: Tropical marine; humid; cooler season during southeast monsoon (late May to September); warmer season during northwest monsoon (March to May)

facts.title: Climate of Sudan
facts.body: Hot and dry; arid desert; rainy season varies by region (April to November)

facts.title: Climate of Sweden
facts.body: Temperate in south with cold, cloudy winters and cool, partly cloudy summers; subarctic in north

facts.title: Climate of Singapore
facts.body: Tropical; hot, humid, rainy; two distinct monsoon seasons - northeastern monsoon (December to March) and southwestern monsoon (June to September); inter-monsoon - frequent afternoon and early evening thunderstorms

facts.title: Climate of Slovenia
facts.body: Mediterranean climate on the coast, continental climate with mild to hot summers and cold winters in the plateaus and valleys to the east

facts.title: Climate of Sierra Leone
facts.body: Tropical; hot, humid; summer rainy season (May to December); winter dry season (December to April)

facts.title: Climate of Senegal
facts.body: Tropical; hot, humid; rainy season (May to November) has strong southeast winds; dry season (December to April) dominated by hot, dry, harmattan wind

facts.title: Climate of Somalia
facts.body: Principally desert; northeast monsoon (December to February), moderate temperatures in north and hot in south; southwest monsoon (May to October), torrid in the north and hot in the south, irregular rainfall, hot and humid periods (tangambili) between monsoons

facts.title: Climate of South Sudan
facts.body: Hot with seasonal rainfall influenced by the annual shift of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone; rainfall heaviest in upland areas of the south and diminishes to the north

facts.title: Climate of El Salvador
facts.body: Tropical; rainy season (May to October); dry season (November to April); tropical on coast; temperate in uplands

facts.title: Climate of Syria
facts.body: Mostly desert; hot, dry, sunny summers (June to August) and mild, rainy winters (December to February) along coast; cold weather with snow or sleet periodically in Damascus

facts.title: Climate of Thailand
facts.body: Tropical; rainy, warm, cloudy southwest monsoon (mid-May to September); dry, cool northeast monsoon (November to mid-March); southern isthmus always hot and humid

facts.title: Climate of Tajikistan
facts.body: Mid-latitude continental, hot summers, mild winters; semiarid to polar in Pamir Mountains

facts.title: Climate of Tunisia
facts.body: Temperate in north with mild, rainy winters and hot, dry summers; desert in south

facts.title: Climate of Tonga
facts.body: Tropical; modified by trade winds; warm season (December to May), cool season (May to December)

facts.title: Climate of Türkiye
facts.body: Temperate; hot, dry summers with mild, wet winters; harsher in interior

facts.title: Climate of Tuvalu
facts.body: Tropical; moderated by easterly trade winds (March to November); westerly gales and heavy rain (November to March)

facts.title: Climate of Ukraine
facts.body: Temperate continental; Mediterranean only on the southern Crimean coast; precipitation disproportionately distributed, highest in west and north, lesser in east and southeast; winters vary from cool along the Black Sea to cold farther inland; warm summers across the greater part of the country, hot in the south

facts.title: Climate of Uganda
facts.body: Tropical; generally rainy with two dry seasons (December to February, June to August); semiarid in northeast

facts.title: Climate of United States
facts.body: Mostly temperate, but tropical in Hawaii and Florida, arctic in Alaska, semiarid in the great plains west of the Mississippi River, and arid in the Great Basin of the southwest; low winter temperatures in the northwest are ameliorated occasionally in January and February by warm chinook winds from the eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountains

facts.title: Climate of Uzbekistan
facts.body: Mostly mid-latitude desert, long, hot summers, mild winters; semiarid grassland in east

facts.title: Climate of Vatican City
facts.body: Temperate; mild, rainy winters (September to May) with hot, dry summers (May to September)

facts.title: Climate of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
facts.body: Tropical; little seasonal temperature variation; rainy season (May to November)

facts.title: Climate of Vietnam
facts.body: Tropical in south; monsoonal in north with hot, rainy season (May to September) and warm, dry season (October to March)

facts.title: Climate of Vanuatu
facts.body: Tropical; moderated by southeast trade winds from May to October; moderate rainfall from November to April; may be affected by cyclones from December to April

facts.title: Climate of Samoa
facts.body: Tropical; rainy season (November to April), dry season (May to October)

facts.title: Climate of Yemen
facts.body: Mostly desert; hot and humid along west coast; temperate in western mountains affected by seasonal monsoon; extraordinarily hot, dry, harsh desert in east

facts.title: Climate of South Africa
facts.body: Mostly semiarid; subtropical along east coast; sunny days, cool nights

facts.title: Climate of Zimbabwe
facts.body: Tropical; moderated by altitude; rainy season (November to March)

facts.title: A geography lesson on toast.
facts.body: Avocados connect a familiar ingredient to a concentrated growing region. Mexico was the largest producer in the 2024 FAO data, growing about 25% of the world total. That makes it a useful place to remember, but a production ranking cannot tell you where a specific brand buys its ingredients.
facts.question: Which country was the largest producer of avocados in 2024?

facts.title: Before the café, there is a country.
facts.body: Coffee has a geography long before it reaches a cup. Brazil was the largest producer in the 2024 FAO data, growing about 30% of the world total. That makes it a useful place to remember, but a production ranking cannot tell you where a specific brand buys its ingredients.
facts.question: Which country was the largest producer of coffee, green in 2024?

facts.title: The country behind the crunch.
facts.body: Hazelnuts have a surprisingly concentrated production map. Türkiye was the largest producer in the 2024 FAO data, growing about 59% of the world total. That makes it a useful place to remember, but a production ranking cannot tell you where a specific brand buys its ingredients.
facts.question: Which country was the largest producer of hazelnuts in 2024?

facts.title: The map behind a handful of pistachios.
facts.body: Pistachio orchards are far from evenly spread around the world. United States was the largest producer in the 2024 FAO data, growing about 36% of the world total. That makes it a useful place to remember, but a production ranking cannot tell you where a specific brand buys its ingredients.
facts.question: Which country was the largest producer of pistachios in 2024?

facts.title: Read the flag of Andorra
facts.body: Three vertical bands of blue (left side), yellow, and red, with the national coat of arms centered in the yellow band, which is slightly wider than the other two; the coat of arms features a quartered shield with the emblems of Urgell, Foix, Bearn, and Catalonia; the motto reads VIRTUS UNITA FORTIOR (Strength United is Stronger)

facts.title: Read the flag of United Arab Emirates
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of green (top), white, and black, with a wider vertical red band on the left side

facts.title: Read the flag of Afghanistan
facts.body: Three equal vertical bands of black (left), red, and green, with the national emblem in white centered on the red band and slightly overlapping the other bands; the emblem shows a mosque with a pulpit and flags on either side; below the mosque are Eastern Arabic numerals for the solar year 1298 (1919 in the Gregorian calendar, the year of Afghan independence from the UK); a border of wheat sheaves circles the mosque; above the mosque is an Arabic inscription of the Shahada (Muslim creed), with rays of the rising sun over the Takbir (Arabic expression meaning "God is great"); under the mosque is a scroll with the name Afghanistan

facts.title: Read the flag of Antigua and Barbuda
facts.body: Red, with an inverted isosceles triangle in the center that spans the flag from top to bottom; the triangle contains three horizontal bands of black (top), light blue, and white, with a yellow rising sun in the black band

facts.title: Read the flag of Angola
facts.body: Two equal horizontal bands of red (top) and black with a centered yellow emblem of a five-pointed star inside half a cogwheel, crossed by a machete (in the style of a hammer and sickle)

facts.title: Read the flag of Argentina
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of sky blue (top), white, and sky blue; centered in the white band is a radiant yellow sun with a human face that is known as the Sun of May

facts.title: Read the flag of Australia
facts.body: Blue, with the UK flag in the upper-left quadrant and a large seven-pointed star in the lower-left quadrant; on the right half is a representation of the Southern Cross constellation in white, with one small five-pointed star and four larger seven-pointed stars

facts.title: Read the flag of Azerbaijan
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of sky blue (top), red, and green; a vertical crescent moon and an eight-pointed star in white are centered in the red band

facts.title: Read the flag of Bosnia and Herzegovina
facts.body: A wide blue vertical band on the right side, with a large yellow isosceles triangle in the middle of the flag, based at the top; the rest of the flag is blue, with seven five-pointed white stars and two half-stars along the triangle's hypotenuse

facts.title: Read the flag of Barbados
facts.body: Three equal vertical bands of ultramarine blue (left side), gold, and ultramarine blue with a black trident head centered on the gold band

facts.title: Read the flag of Burkina Faso
facts.body: Two equal horizontal bands of red (top) and green, with a five-pointed yellow star in the center

facts.title: Read the flag of Burundi
facts.body: Divided by a white diagonal cross into red triangles (top and bottom) and green triangles (on each side) with a white disk at the center bearing three six-pointed red stars outlined in green and arranged in a triangular design

facts.title: Read the flag of Benin
facts.body: Two equal horizontal bands of yellow (top) and red (bottom) to the right, with a vertical green band on the left side

facts.title: Read the flag of Brunei
facts.body: Yellow with a diagonal white band and second below it in black, both starting from the upper left; the national emblem in red is at the center; the state motto, "Always render service with God's guidance," appears in yellow Arabic script on the emblem's crescent; a ribbon below the crescent reads "Brunei, the Abode of Peace"

facts.title: Read the flag of Bolivia
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of red (top), yellow, and green, with the coat of arms centered on the yellow band

facts.title: Read the flag of Brazil
facts.body: Green with a large yellow diamond in the center, showing a blue celestial globe with 27 five-pointed white stars; the globe has a white equatorial band with the motto ORDEM E PROGRESSO (Order and Progress)

facts.title: Read the flag of Bahamas
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of aquamarine (top), gold, and aquamarine, with a black equilateral triangle based on the left side

facts.title: Read the flag of Bhutan
facts.body: Divided diagonally from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner; the upper triangle is yellow, and the lower triangle is dark orange; centered along the dividing line is a large, stylized black-and-white dragon facing to the right; the dragon is called the Druk (Thunder Dragon) and is the national emblem

facts.title: Read the flag of Botswana
facts.body: Light blue with a horizontal white-edged black stripe across the middle

facts.title: Read the flag of Belarus
facts.body: Red horizontal band (top), with a green horizontal band below that is half the width of the red band; a white vertical stripe on the left side has traditional Belarusian designs in red

facts.title: Read the flag of Belize
facts.body: Royal blue with a narrow red stripe along the top and the bottom edges; the coat of arms is on a large white disk at the center and shows a shield flanked by two workers in front of a mahogany tree, with the motto SUB UMBRA FLOREO (I Flourish in the Shade) on a scroll at the bottom; a green garland of 50 mahogany leaves rings the coat of arms

facts.title: Read the flag of Canada
facts.body: Two vertical bands of red on each side, with a white square between them; a large 11-pointed red maple leaf is centered in the white square

facts.title: Read the flag of Democratic Republic of the Congo
facts.body: Sky-blue field divided diagonally from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner by a red stripe bordered with two narrow yellow stripes; a five-pointed yellow star is in the upper-left corner

facts.title: Read the flag of Central African Republic
facts.body: Four equal horizontal bands of blue (top), white, green, and yellow with a vertical red band in the center; a five-pointed yellow star sits in the top left corner of the flag, on the blue band

facts.title: Read the flag of Republic of the Congo
facts.body: Divided diagonally from the lower-left side by a wide yellow band; the upper triangle (left side) is green, and the lower triangle is red

facts.title: Read the flag of Switzerland
facts.body: Red square with an equal-armed white cross in the center that does not extend to the edges of the flag

facts.title: Read the flag of Chile
facts.body: Two equal horizontal bands of white (top) and red; a blue square sits in the top left corner of the flag, the same height as the white band; the square has a five-pointed white star in the center

facts.title: Read the flag of Cameroon
facts.body: Three equal vertical bands of green (left side), red, and yellow, with a small five-pointed yellow star centered in the red band

facts.title: Read the flag of China
facts.body: Red with a large five-pointed yellow star and four smaller ones in the upper-left corner; the small stars are arranged in a vertical arc around the large one

facts.title: Read the flag of Costa Rica
facts.body: Five horizontal bands of blue (top), white, red (double-width), white, and blue, with the coat of arms in a white elliptical disk placed toward the left side of the red band

facts.title: Read the flag of Cuba
facts.body: Five equal horizontal bands of blue (top, center, and bottom) alternating with white; a red equilateral triangle based on the left side has a five-pointed white star in the center

facts.title: Read the flag of Cape Verde
facts.body: Five unequal horizontal bands; the top band of blue is half the height of the flag; under it are three narrow bands of white, red, and white, and a bottom stripe of blue; a circle of 10 five-pointed yellow stars is centered on the red stripe and sits toward the left side of the flag

facts.title: Read the flag of Cyprus
facts.body: A copper-colored silhouette of the island is centered on a white field above two crossed green olive branches

facts.title: Read the flag of Czechia
facts.body: Two equal horizontal bands of white (top) and red with a blue isosceles triangle based on the left side

facts.title: Read the flag of Djibouti
facts.body: Two equal horizontal bands of light blue (top) and light green, with a white isosceles triangle based on the left side that has a five-pointed red star in the center

facts.title: Read the flag of Denmark
facts.body: Red field with a white cross that extends to the edges of the flag; the vertical part of the cross is shifted to the left

facts.title: Read the flag of Dominica
facts.body: Green with a centered cross of three equal bands in yellow, black, and white; in the center of the cross is a red disk with a Sisserou parrot surrounded by 10 five-pointed green stars edged in yellow

facts.title: Read the flag of Dominican Republic
facts.body: A centered white cross extends to the edges and divides the flag into four rectangles; the top ones are ultramarine blue (left side) and vermilion red, and the bottom ones are vermilion red (left side) and ultramarine blue; a small coat of arms with a shield supported by a laurel branch and a palm branch is at the center of the cross; above the shield, a blue ribbon displays the motto DIOS, PATRIA, LIBERTAD (God, Fatherland, Liberty); below the shield, REPUBLICA DOMINICANA is on a red ribbon; on the shield, a Bible is opened to a verse that reads "Y la verdad nos hara libre" (And the truth shall set you free)

facts.title: Read the flag of Algeria
facts.body: Two equal vertical bands of green (left) and white; a red, five-pointed star inside a red crescent, centered over the two-color boundary

facts.title: Read the flag of Ecuador
facts.body: Three horizontal bands of yellow (top, double-width), blue, and red, with the coat of arms at the center of the flag

facts.title: Read the flag of Egypt
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of red (top), white, and black; centered in the white band is the national emblem, a gold Eagle of Saladin; it faces the left side, with a shield on its chest, above a scroll with the country's name in Arabic

facts.title: Read the flag of Eritrea
facts.body: A red isosceles triangle (based on the left side) divides the flag into two right triangles; the upper triangle is green, the lower is blue; a gold wreath around a gold olive branch is on the left side of the red triangle

facts.title: Read the flag of Spain
facts.body: Three horizontal bands of red (top), yellow (double-width), and red, with the national coat of arms on the left side of the yellow band; the coat of arms shows the emblems of the area's former kingdoms (clockwise from upper left: Castile, Leon, Navarre, and Aragon), which also used red and yellow as their colors; the stylized pomegranate at the bottom of the shield represents Granada; the two columns represent the Pillars of Hercules, which are promontories (Gibraltar and Ceuta) on the Strait of Gibraltar; a red scroll bears the imperial motto of "Plus Ultra" (further beyond), referring to Spanish lands outside Europe

facts.title: Read the flag of Ethiopia
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of green (top), yellow, and red, with a light blue disk centered on the three bands; on the disk is a yellow pentagram with single yellow rays emanating from the angles between the points

facts.title: Read the flag of Finland
facts.body: White with a blue cross extending to the edges of the flag; the cross is shifted to the left in the style of the Dannebrog (Danish flag)

facts.title: Read the flag of Fiji
facts.body: Light blue with the UK flag in the upper-left quadrant and the Fijian shield centered on the right half of the flag; the shield shows a yellow lion holding a coconut above a white field quartered by the cross of Saint George; the four quarters depict sugarcane, a palm tree, a banana bunch, and a white dove

facts.title: Read the flag of Micronesia
facts.body: Light blue with four five-pointed white stars centered and arranged in a diamond pattern

facts.title: Read the flag of United Kingdom
facts.body: Blue field with the red cross of Saint George (patron saint of England) edged in white on top of the diagonal red cross of Saint Patrick (patron saint of Ireland), which is on top of the diagonal white cross of Saint Andrew (patron saint of Scotland)

facts.title: Read the flag of Grenada
facts.body: A rectangle divided diagonally into yellow triangles (top and bottom) and green triangles (left and right), with a wide red border around the flag; three five-pointed yellow stars are centered on the top and bottom of the red border, with one larger yellow star on a red disk at the center of the flag; a small yellow-and-red nutmeg pod is on the left triangle

facts.title: Read the flag of Georgia
facts.body: White rectangle with a central red cross extending to all four sides of the flag; each of the four quadrants displays a small red bolnur-katskhuri cross (also known as Bolnisi cross), which has equal-length arms that are slightly wider at the end than in the center

facts.title: Read the flag of Ghana
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of red (top), yellow, and green, with a large five-pointed black star centered in the yellow band

facts.title: Read the flag of Gambia
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of red (top), blue with white edges, and green

facts.title: Read the flag of Equatorial Guinea
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of green (top), white, and red, with a blue isosceles triangle based on the left side and the coat of arms centered in the white band; the coat of arms has six six-pointed yellow stars (representing the mainland and five offshore islands) above a gray shield with a silk-cotton tree; below is a scroll with the motto UNIDAD, PAZ, JUSTICIA (Unity, Peace, Justice)

facts.title: Read the flag of Greece
facts.body: Nine equal horizontal stripes of blue alternating with white; a blue square with a white cross is in the upper-left corner

facts.title: Read the flag of Guatemala
facts.body: Three equal vertical bands of light blue (left side), white, and light blue, with the coat of arms centered in the white band; the coat of arms includes a green-and-red quetzal (the national bird), a scroll with the inscription LIBERTAD 15 DE SEPTIEMBRE DE 1821 (the original date of independence from Spain), a pair of crossed rifles, and a pair of crossed swords; a laurel wreath frames the objects

facts.title: Read the flag of Guinea-Bissau
facts.body: Two equal horizontal bands of yellow (top) and green, with a vertical red band on the left side; a five-pointed black star is centered in the red band

facts.title: Read the flag of Guyana
facts.body: Green with a red isosceles triangle (based on the left side) on top of a long yellow arrowhead shape that extends to the opposite side of the flag; a narrow black border sits between the red and yellow, and a narrow white border between the yellow and green

facts.title: Read the flag of Honduras
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of cerulean blue (top), white, and cerulean blue, with five five-pointed cerulean stars arranged in an "X" pattern and centered in the white band

facts.title: Read the flag of Croatia
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of red (top), white, and blue -- the pan-Slav colors -- with the Croatian coat of arms in the center, which consists of a main shield (a checkerboard of 13 red and 12 silver fields) with five smaller shields that form a crown over the main shield

facts.title: Read the flag of Haiti
facts.body: Two equal horizontal bands of blue (top) and red; a centered white rectangle bears the coat of arms, which has a palm tree flanked by flags and two cannons above a scroll with the motto L'UNION FAIT LA FORCE (Union Makes Strength)

facts.title: Read the flag of Israel
facts.body: White with a blue hexagram (six-pointed linear star) known as the Magen David (Star of David or Shield of David) centered between two equal horizontal blue bands near the top and bottom edges of the flag

facts.title: Read the flag of India
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of saffron (top), white, and green, with a blue chakra (24-spoked wheel) centered in the white band

facts.title: Read the flag of Iraq
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of red (top), white, and black; the Takbir (Arabic phrase meaning "God is great") in green Arabic script is centered in the white band

facts.title: Read the flag of Iran
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of green (top), white, and red; centered in the white band is the red national emblem, a stylization of the word Allah in the shape of a tulip (a symbol of martyrdom); ALLAH AKBAR (God is Great) in white Arabic script is repeated 11 times along the bottom edge of the green band and 11 times along the top edge of the red band

facts.title: Read the flag of Iceland
facts.body: Blue with a red cross outlined in white extending to the edges of the flag; the cross is shifted to the left in the style of the Dannebrog (Danish flag)

facts.title: Read the flag of Jamaica
facts.body: Diagonal yellow cross divides the flag into four triangles, two green (top and bottom) and two black (left and right)

facts.title: Read the flag of Jordan
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of black (top), white, and green; a red isosceles triangle is on the left side, with a small white seven-pointed star in the center

facts.title: Read the flag of Japan
facts.body: White with a large red disk that symbolizes the sun without rays, in the center

facts.title: Read the flag of Kenya
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of black (top), red, and green; the red band is edged in white; a large Maasai warrior's shield covering crossed spears is at the center

facts.title: Read the flag of Kyrgyzstan
facts.body: Red field with a yellow sun in the center that has 40 rays that run counterclockwise on the front of the flag and clockwise on the reverse; in the center of the sun is a red ring crossed by two sets of three lines in a stylized representation of a tunduk, the circular opening at the top of a traditional Kyrgyz yurt

facts.title: Read the flag of Cambodia
facts.body: Three horizontal bands of blue (top), red (double-width), and blue; a three-towered, stylized white temple outlined in black is in the center of the red band, representing Angkor Wat

facts.title: Read the flag of Kiribati
facts.body: The upper half is red with a yellow frigatebird flying over a yellow rising sun, and the lower half is blue with three wavy horizontal white stripes to represent the Pacific Ocean

facts.title: Read the flag of Comoros
facts.body: Four equal horizontal bands of yellow (top), white, red, and blue, with a green isosceles triangle based on the left; a vertical white crescent moon is centered in the triangle, with four five-pointed white stars placed vertically in a line between the points of the crescent

facts.title: Read the flag of Saint Kitts and Nevis
facts.body: Divided diagonally from the lower left side by a broad black band with two five-pointed white stars; the black band is edged in yellow; the upper triangle is green, and the lower is red

facts.title: Read the flag of North Korea
facts.body: Three horizontal bands of blue (top), red (triple-width), and blue; the red band is edged in white; on the left side of the red band is a white disk with a red five-pointed star

facts.title: Read the flag of South Korea
facts.body: White with a red-and-blue yin-yang symbol in the center; a black trigram ( kwae ) from the ancient I Ching (Book of Changes) is in each corner of the white field

facts.title: Read the flag of Kuwait
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of green (top), white, and red, with a black trapezoid based on the left side

facts.title: Read the flag of Kazakhstan
facts.body: A gold sun with 32 rays above a soaring golden steppe eagle, both centered on a sky-blue background; the left side displays a national pattern called koshkar-muiz (the horns of the ram) in gold

facts.title: Read the flag of Laos
facts.body: Three horizontal bands of red (top), blue (double-width), and red, with a large white disk centered in the blue band

facts.title: Read the flag of Lebanon
facts.body: Three horizontal bands consisting of red (top), white (middle, double-width), and red (bottom), with a green cedar tree centered on the white band

facts.title: Read the flag of Saint Lucia
facts.body: Cerulean blue with a gold isosceles triangle below a black arrowhead; the upper edges of the arrowhead have a white border

facts.title: Read the flag of Liechtenstein
facts.body: Two equal horizontal bands of blue (top) and red, with a gold crown on the left side of the blue band

facts.title: Read the flag of Sri Lanka
facts.body: Yellow with two panels; the smaller panel on the left has two equal vertical bands of green (left side) and orange; the larger panel has a yellow lion holding a sword on a maroon field, with a yellow bo leaf in each corner

facts.title: Read the flag of Liberia
facts.body: 11 equal horizontal stripes of red alternating with white; a five-pointed white star sits on a blue square in the upper-left corner

facts.title: Read the flag of Lesotho
facts.body: Three horizontal stripes of blue (top), white, and green; centered on the white stripe is a black mokorotlo , a traditional Basotho straw hat and national symbol

facts.title: Read the flag of Latvia
facts.body: Three horizontal bands of maroon (top), white (half-width), and maroon

facts.title: Read the flag of Libya
facts.body: Three horizontal bands of red (top), black (double-width), and green, with a white crescent and star centered on the black stripe

facts.title: Read the flag of Morocco
facts.body: Red with a green pentacle (five-pointed linear star) known as Sulayman's (Solomon's) seal in the center of the flag

facts.title: Read the flag of Moldova
facts.body: Three equal vertical bands of Prussian blue (left side), chrome yellow, and vermilion red; the Moldavan coat of arms in the center is a dark gold Roman eagle outlined in black, with a red beak and talons; the eagle carries a yellow cross in its beak, a green olive branch in its right talons, and a yellow scepter in its left talons; on the eagle's breast is a red-and-blue shield divided horizontally, with a stylized aurochs head, star, rose, and crescent in black and outlined yellow; the reverse of the flag displays a mirror image of the coat of arms

facts.title: Read the flag of Montenegro
facts.body: A red field bordered with a narrow golden-yellow stripe; the Montenegrin coat of arms in the center is a double-headed golden eagle, with a crown above; the eagle holds a golden scepter in its right claw and a blue orb in its left; the eagle's breast shield shows a golden lion on a green field in front of a blue sky

facts.title: Read the flag of Madagascar
facts.body: Two equal horizontal bands of red (top) and green, with a vertical white band on the left side

facts.title: Read the flag of Marshall Islands
facts.body: Blue with an orange stripe and a white stripe radiating from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner; a white star with four large rays and 20 small rays appears on the left side above the two stripes

facts.title: Read the flag of North Macedonia
facts.body: A red field with a yellow sun (the Sun of Liberty) in the center, with eight broadening rays extending to the edges

facts.title: Read the flag of Myanmar
facts.body: Three equal horizontal stripes of yellow (top), green, and red; centered on the green band is a five-pointed white star that overlaps onto the yellow and red stripes

facts.title: Read the flag of Mongolia
facts.body: Three equal vertical bands of red (left side), blue, and red; centered on the left-side red band is the national emblem in yellow, the soyombo, which is an abstract representation of fire, sun, moon, earth, water, and the yin-yang symbol

facts.title: Read the flag of Mauritania
facts.body: Green with red stripes along the top and bottom edges; on the green field, a five-pointed yellow star is centered over a yellow, upward-pointing crescent moon

facts.title: Read the flag of Malta
facts.body: Two equal vertical bands of white (left side) and red; in the upper-left corner is the George Cross, edged in red

facts.title: Read the flag of Maldives
facts.body: Red with a large green rectangle in the center and a vertical white crescent moon centered on the rectangle

facts.title: Read the flag of Malawi
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of black (top), red, and green, with a rising red sun centered on the black band

facts.title: Read the flag of Mexico
facts.body: Three equal vertical bands of green (left side), white, and red; Mexico's coat of arms (an eagle with a snake in its beak, perched on a cactus) is centered in the white band

facts.title: Read the flag of Malaysia
facts.body: 14 equal horizontal stripes of red alternating with white; a dark blue rectangle in the upper-left corner has a yellow crescent and a 14-pointed yellow star

facts.title: Read the flag of Mozambique
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of green (top), black, and yellow, with a red isosceles triangle based on the left side; the black band is edged in white; centered in the triangle is a five-pointed yellow star with a crossed black-and-white rifle and hoe, on top of an open white book

facts.title: Read the flag of Namibia
facts.body: A wide red stripe edged with narrow white stripes divides the flag diagonally from lower-left corner to upper-right corner; the upper triangle is blue and has a golden-yellow, 12-ray sunburst, and the lower triangle is green

facts.title: Read the flag of Niger
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of orange (top), white, and green, with an orange disk centered on the white band

facts.title: Read the flag of Nicaragua
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of blue (top), white, and blue, with the national coat of arms centered in the white band; the coat of arms has a triangle with the words REPUBLICA DE NICARAGUA in an arc over it and AMERICA CENTRAL in an arc underneath

facts.title: Read the flag of Netherlands
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of bright red (top), white, and cobalt blue

facts.title: Read the flag of Norway
facts.body: Red with a blue cross outlined in white that extends to the edges of the flag; the the cross is shifted to the left side in the style of the Dannebrog (Danish flag)

facts.title: Read the flag of Nepal
facts.body: Crimson red with a blue border, in the shape of two overlapping right triangles; the smaller upper triangle has a stylized white moon, and the larger lower triangle has a 12-pointed white sun

facts.title: Read the flag of Nauru
facts.body: Blue with a narrow horizontal gold stripe across the center and a large white 12-pointed star below the stripe on the left side

facts.title: Read the flag of New Zealand
facts.body: Blue with the UK flag in the upper-left quadrant, with four five-pointed red stars edged in white centered in the right half of the flag

facts.title: Read the flag of Oman
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of white (top), red, and green, with a vertical red band on the left side; the national emblem (a khanjar dagger in its sheath on top of crossed swords in scabbards) in white is centered near the top of the vertical band

facts.title: Read the flag of Panama
facts.body: Divided into four equal rectangles; one of the top quadrants is white (left side) with a five-pointed blue star in the center, and the other is plain red; one of the bottom quadrants is plain blue (left side), and the other is white with a five-pointed red star in the center

facts.title: Read the flag of Peru
facts.body: Three equal vertical bands of red (left side), white, and red, with the coat of arms centered on the white band; the coat of arms has a shield with a vicuna, a cinchona tree, and a yellow cornucopia spilling out coins

facts.title: Read the flag of Papua New Guinea
facts.body: Divided diagonally from upper-left corner; the upper triangle is red and has a soaring yellow bird of paradise in the center; the lower triangle is black with five five-pointed white stars of the Southern Cross constellation

facts.title: Read the flag of Philippines
facts.body: Two equal horizontal bands of blue (top) and red; a white equilateral triangle is based on the left side; the center of the triangle has a yellow sun with eight rays, each split into smaller rays; the triangle's corners each have a small five-pointed yellow star

facts.title: Read the flag of Pakistan
facts.body: Green with a vertical white band on the left side; a large white crescent and star are centered in the green field

facts.title: Read the flag of Palestine
facts.body: Three horizontal stripes of black, white and green meet a red triangle at the hoist. These four colours are shared with several other Arab flags.

facts.title: Read the flag of Portugal
facts.body: Two vertical bands of green (left side, two-fifths) and red (three-fifths), with the national coat of arms (armillary sphere and national shield) centered on the dividing line

facts.title: Read the flag of Paraguay
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of red (top), white, and blue, with an emblem centered on the white band; the emblem on one side of the flag is the national coat of arms, which has a five-pointed yellow star in a green wreath with the words REPUBLICA DEL PARAGUAY around it, all inside two circles; the other side of the flag has a circular treasury seal (a yellow lion below a red Cap of Liberty and the words PAZ Y JUSTICIA)

facts.title: Read the flag of Serbia
facts.body: Three equal horizontal stripes of red (top), blue, and white; the national coat of arms is shifted to the left side; the principal field of the coat of arms displays a two-headed white eagle on a red shield; a smaller red shield on the eagle is divided into four quarters by a white cross; a royal crown is on top of the coat of arms

facts.title: Read the flag of Rwanda
facts.body: Three horizontal bands of sky blue (top, double-width), yellow, and green, with a golden sun with 24 rays on the right end of the blue band

facts.title: Read the flag of Saudi Arabia
facts.body: Green (traditional Islamic color) with the Shahada, or Muslim creed, in large white Arabic script that translates as, "There is no god but God; Muhammad is the messenger of God;" the text is above a white horizontal saber pointing to the left

facts.title: Read the flag of Solomon Islands
facts.body: Divided diagonally by a yellow stripe from the lower-left corner; the upper triangle (left side) is blue with five five-pointed white stars in an "X" pattern; the lower triangle is green

facts.title: Read the flag of Seychelles
facts.body: Five expanding bands of blue, yellow, red, white, and green, radiating from the bottom left corner

facts.title: Read the flag of Sudan
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of red (top), white, and black, with a green isosceles triangle based on the left side

facts.title: Read the flag of Sweden
facts.body: Blue with a golden yellow cross extending to the edges of the flag; the cross is shifted to the left side in the style of the Dannebrog (Danish flag)

facts.title: Read the flag of Singapore
facts.body: Two equal horizontal bands of red (top) and white; a vertical white crescent is on the left side of the red band, with a circle of five five-pointed white stars to the right of the crescent

facts.title: Read the flag of Slovenia
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of white (top), blue, and red; the Slovenian seal (a shield with Triglav, the country's highest peak, in white on a blue background) is at the center, with two wavy blue lines under it; three six-pointed stars in an inverted triangle appear on the upper-left

facts.title: Read the flag of Slovakia
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of white (top), blue, and red; the national coat of arms (a red shield bordered in white, with a white double-barred cross of St. Cyril and St. Methodius on top of three blue hills) is centered over the bands but offset to the left

facts.title: Read the flag of Sierra Leone
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of light green (top), white, and light blue

facts.title: Read the flag of San Marino
facts.body: Two equal horizontal bands of white (top) and light blue, with the national coat of arms in the center; the main colors come from the shield on the coat of arms, which features three white towers on mountain peaks on a blue field; a wreath and a crown are around the shield, above a scroll with the word LIBERTAS (Liberty)

facts.title: Read the flag of Senegal
facts.body: Three equal vertical bands of green (left side), yellow, and red, with a small five-pointed green star centered on the yellow band; green stands for Islam, progress, and hope, yellow for natural wealth and progress, and red for sacrifice and determination; the star represents unity and hope

facts.title: Read the flag of Suriname
facts.body: Five horizontal bands of green (top, double-width), white, red (quadruple-width), white, and green (double-width); a five-pointed yellow star is centered on the red band

facts.title: Read the flag of South Sudan
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of black (top), red, and green; the red band is edged in white; a five-pointed gold star is in the middle of a blue isosceles triangle based on the left side

facts.title: Read the flag of São Tomé and Príncipe
facts.body: Three horizontal bands of green (top), yellow (double-width), and green with two five-pointed black stars in the center of the yellow band and a red isosceles triangle based on the left side

facts.title: Read the flag of El Salvador
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of cobalt blue (top), white, and cobalt blue, with the national coat of arms centered in the white band; the coat of arms has a round emblem with the words REPUBLICA DE EL SALVADOR EN LA AMERICA CENTRAL around it

facts.title: Read the flag of Syria
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of green (top), white, and black; three five-pointed red stars in a horizontal line, centered on the white band

facts.title: Read the flag of Eswatini
facts.body: Three horizontal bands of blue (top), red (triple-width), and blue; the red band is edged in yellow, with a large black-and-white shield in the center that covers two horizontal spears and a staff with feather tassels

facts.title: Read the flag of Togo
facts.body: Five equal horizontal bands of green (top and bottom) alternating with yellow; a five-pointed white star on a red square is in the upper-left corner

facts.title: Read the flag of Thailand
facts.body: Five horizontal bands of red (top), white, blue (double-width), white, and red

facts.title: Read the flag of Tajikistan
facts.body: Three horizontal stripes of red (top), a wider stripe of white, and green; a gold crown under seven five-pointed gold stars is in the center of the white stripe

facts.title: Read the flag of Timor-Leste
facts.body: Red with a black isosceles triangle (based on the left side) on a slightly longer yellow arrowhead that extends to the center of the flag; a white star is in the center of the black triangle

facts.title: Read the flag of Turkmenistan
facts.body: Green field with a vertical red stripe near the left side; the stripe has five tribal guls (designs used in producing carpets) stacked above two crossed olive branches; five five-pointed white stars and a white crescent moon appear in the upper left corner of the main field

facts.title: Read the flag of Tunisia
facts.body: Red with a white disk in the center that displays a red crescent around a five-pointed red star

facts.title: Read the flag of Türkiye
facts.body: Red with a vertical white crescent moon and five-pointed white star centered just outside the crescent's opening

facts.title: Read the flag of Trinidad and Tobago
facts.body: Red with a white-edged black diagonal band from the upper left to the lower right

facts.title: Read the flag of Tuvalu
facts.body: Light blue with the UK flag in the upper-left quadrant; the right half of the flag has nine five-pointed yellow stars

facts.title: Read the flag of Tanzania
facts.body: Divided diagonally by a yellow-edged black band, from the lower left corner to the upper right corner; the upper triangle (left side) is green, and the lower is blue

facts.title: Read the flag of Uganda
facts.body: Six equal horizontal bands of black (top), yellow, red, black, yellow, and red; a white disk is at the center and shows a grey crowned crane (the national symbol)

facts.title: Read the flag of United States
facts.body: 13 equal horizontal stripes of red (top and bottom) alternating with white; a blue rectangle in the upper-left corner has 50 five-pointed white stars, arranged in nine offset horizontal rows of six stars (top and bottom) alternating with rows of five stars

facts.title: Read the flag of Uruguay
facts.body: Nine equal horizontal stripes of white (top and bottom) alternating with blue; a white square in the upper-left corner has a yellow sun with a human face (outlined in black) known as the Sun of May, with 16 rays that alternate between triangular and wavy

facts.title: Read the flag of Uzbekistan
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of blue (top), white, and green separated by narrow red stripes with a vertical white crescent moon and 12 five-pointed white stars in the left corner of the top band

facts.title: Read the flag of Vatican City
facts.body: Two vertical bands of yellow (left side) and white, with the arms of the Holy See centered in the white band; the arms show the crossed keys of Saint Peter under the three-tiered papal tiara

facts.title: Read the flag of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
facts.body: Three vertical bands of blue (left side), gold (double-width), and green; the gold band has three green diamonds arranged in a "V" pattern that stands for "Vincent"

facts.title: Read the flag of Venezuela
facts.body: Three equal horizontal bands of yellow (top), blue, and red, with the coat of arms on the left side of the yellow band and an arc of eight five-pointed white stars centered on the blue band

facts.title: Read the flag of Vanuatu
facts.body: Two equal horizontal bands of red (top) and green with a black isosceles triangle (based on the left side); a black-edged yellow stripe in the shape of a horizontal "Y" faces the left side and encloses the triangle; a boar's tusk in the triangle circles two crossed namele fern fronds, all in yellow

facts.title: Read the flag of Samoa
facts.body: Red with a blue rectangle in the upper-left quadrant; on the rectangle are five five-pointed white stars that represent the Southern Cross constellation

facts.title: Read the flag of South Africa
facts.body: Two equal-width horizontal bands of red (top) and blue separated by a central green band that splits into a horizontal Y; a black isosceles triangle is in the Y, with narrow yellow bands around it; the red and blue bands are bordered by narrow white stripes

facts.title: Read the flag of Zambia
facts.body: Green field with a soaring orange eagle in the upper-right corner; a panel of three vertical bands is under the eagle, in red (left side), black, and orange

facts.title: Read the flag of Zimbabwe
facts.body: Seven equal horizontal bands of green (top), yellow, red, black, red, yellow, and green, with a white isosceles triangle edged in black based on the left side; in the middle of the triangle, a yellow bird is on top of a five-pointed red star

facts.title: Geography of Andorra
facts.body: Landlocked; straddles a number of important crossroads in the Pyrenees

facts.title: Geography of United Arab Emirates
facts.body: Strategic location along southern approaches to Strait of Hormuz, a transit point for crude oil; Abu Zaby (Abu Dhabi) and Dubayy (Dubai) together account for over 90% of UAE's area and two-thirds of the population

facts.title: Geography of Afghanistan
facts.body: Landlocked; the Hindu Kush mountains that run northeast to southwest divide the northern provinces from the rest of the country; the highest peaks are in the northern Vakhan (Wakhan Corridor)

facts.title: Geography of Antigua and Barbuda
facts.body: Antigua has a deeply indented shoreline with many natural harbors and beaches; Barbuda has a large western harbor

facts.title: Geography of Albania
facts.body: Strategic location along Strait of Otranto (links Adriatic Sea to Ionian Sea and Mediterranean Sea)

facts.title: Geography of Armenia
facts.body: Landlocked in the Lesser Caucasus Mountains; Sevana Lich (Lake Sevan) is the largest lake in this mountain range

facts.title: Geography of Angola
facts.body: The province of Cabinda is an exclave, separated from the rest of the country by the Democratic Republic of the Congo

facts.title: Geography of Argentina
facts.body: Second-largest country in South America (after Brazil); strategic location relative to sea lanes between the South Atlantic and the South Pacific Oceans (Strait of Magellan, Beagle Channel, Drake Passage); diverse geophysical landscapes range from tropical climates in the north to tundra in the far south; Cerro Aconcagua is the Western Hemisphere's tallest mountain, while Laguna del Carbón is the lowest point in the Western Hemisphere; shares Iguazú Falls, the world's largest waterfalls system, with Brazil

facts.title: Geography of Austria
facts.body: Landlocked; strategic location at the crossroads of central Europe with many easily traversable Alpine passes and valleys; major river is the Danube; population is concentrated on eastern lowlands because of steep slopes, poor soils, and low temperatures elsewhere

facts.title: Geography of Austria
facts.body: The world's largest and longest ice cave system at 42 km (26 mi) is the Eisriesenwelt (Ice Giants World) inside the Hochkogel mountain near Werfen, about 40 km south of Salzburg; ice caves are bedrock caves that contain year-round ice formations; they differ from glacial caves, which are transient and are formed by melting ice and flowing water within and under glaciers

facts.title: Geography of Australia
facts.body: World's smallest continent but sixth-largest country; the largest country in Oceania, the largest country entirely in the Southern Hemisphere, and the largest country without land borders

facts.title: Geography of Australia
facts.body: The Great Dividing Range that runs along eastern Australia is that continent’s longest mountain range and the third-longest land-based range in the world; the term "Great Dividing Range" refers to the fact that the mountains form a watershed crest from which all of the rivers of eastern Australia flow – east, west, north, and south

facts.title: Geography of Australia
facts.body: Australia is the only continent without glaciers; it is the driest inhabited continent on earth; Perth on the west coast is home to the invigorating sea breeze known as the "Fremantle Doctor," one of the most consistent winds in the world; Australia hosts 10% of the world's biodiversity, and a great number of its flora and fauna exist nowhere else in the world

facts.title: Geography of Azerbaijan
facts.body: Both the main area of the country and the Naxcivan exclave are landlocked

facts.title: Geography of Bosnia and Herzegovina
facts.body: Within Bosnia and Herzegovina's recognized borders, the country is divided into a joint Bosniak/Croat Federation (about 51% of the territory) and the Bosnian Serb-led Republika Srpska or RS (about 49% of the territory); the region called Herzegovina is contiguous to Croatia and Montenegro

facts.title: Geography of Bangladesh
facts.body: Most of the country is situated on deltas of large rivers flowing from the Himalayas: the Ganges unites with the Jamuna (main channel of the Brahmaputra) and later joins the Meghna to eventually empty into the Bay of Bengal

facts.title: Geography of Belgium
facts.body: Crossroads of Western Europe; most West European capitals are within 1,000 km of Brussels, the seat of both the EU and NATO

facts.title: Geography of Burkina Faso
facts.body: Landlocked savanna cut by the three principal rivers, the Black, Red, and White Voltas

facts.title: Geography of Bulgaria
facts.body: Strategic location near Turkish Straits; controls key land routes from Europe to Middle East and Asia

facts.title: Geography of Bahrain
facts.body: Close to primary Middle Eastern petroleum sources; strategic location in Persian Gulf, through which much of the Western world's petroleum must transit to reach open ocean

facts.title: Geography of Burundi
facts.body: Landlocked; straddles crest of the Nile-Congo watershed; the Kagera, which drains into Lake Victoria, is the most remote headstream of the White Nile

facts.title: Geography of Benin
facts.body: Sandbanks create difficult access to a coast with no natural harbors, river mouths, or islands

facts.title: Geography of Brunei
facts.body: Close to vital sea lanes through South China Sea linking Indian and Pacific Oceans; two parts physically separated by Malaysia; the eastern part, the Temburong district, is an exclave and is almost an enclave within Malaysia

facts.title: Geography of Bolivia
facts.body: Landlocked; shares control of Lago Titicaca, world's highest navigable lake (elevation 3,805 m), with Peru

facts.title: Geography of Brazil
facts.body: Largest country in South America and in the Southern Hemisphere; shares common boundaries with every South American country except Chile and Ecuador; most of the Pantanal, the world's largest tropical wetland, extends through the west central part of the country; shares Iguaçu Falls (Iguazú Falls), the world's largest waterfalls system, with Argentina

facts.title: Geography of Brazil
facts.body: Rocas Atoll, located off the northeast coast of Brazil, is the only atoll in the South Atlantic

facts.title: Geography of Bahamas
facts.body: Strategic location adjacent to US and Cuba; extensive island chain of which 30 are inhabited

facts.title: Geography of Bhutan
facts.body: Landlocked; strategic location between China and India; controls several key Himalayan mountain passes

facts.title: Geography of Botswana
facts.body: Landlocked; sparsely populated with most settlement concentrated in the southern and eastern parts of the country; geography dominated by the Kalahari Desert, which covers about 70% of the country, although the Okavango Delta brings considerable biodiversity as one of the largest inland deltas in the World

facts.title: Geography of Belarus
facts.body: Landlocked; glacial scouring accounts for the flatness of Belarusian terrain and for its 11,000 lakes

facts.title: Geography of Belize
facts.body: Only country in Central America without a coastline on the North Pacific Ocean

facts.title: Geography of Canada
facts.body: Second-largest country in the world (after Russia) and largest in the Americas; strategic location between Russia and US via north polar route; approximately 90% of the population is concentrated within 160 km (100 mi) of the US border

facts.title: Geography of Canada
facts.body: Canada has more fresh water than any other country, and almost 9% of Canadian territory is water; Canada has at least 2 million and possibly over 3 million lakes, more than all other countries combined

facts.title: Geography of Democratic Republic of the Congo
facts.body: Second-largest country in Africa (after Algeria) and largest country in sub-Saharan Africa; straddles the equator; dense tropical rainforest in central river basin and eastern highlands; the narrow strip of land that controls the lower Congo River is the DRC's only outlet to the South Atlantic Ocean

facts.title: Geography of Democratic Republic of the Congo
facts.body: The Congo River, most of which flows through the DRC, has never been accurately measured along much of its length because of its speed, cataracts, rapids, and turbulence; nonetheless, it is conceded to be the deepest river in the world, with estimates of the point of greatest depth varying between 220 and 250 meters

facts.title: Geography of Republic of the Congo
facts.body: About 70% of the population lives in Brazzaville, Pointe-Noire, or along the railroad between them

facts.title: Geography of Switzerland
facts.body: Landlocked; crossroads of northern and southern Europe; along with southeastern France, northern Italy, and southwestern Austria, has the highest elevations in the Alps

facts.title: Geography of Côte d’Ivoire
facts.body: Most of the inhabitants live along the sandy coastal region; apart from the capital area, the forested interior is sparsely populated

facts.title: Geography of Chile
facts.body: Chile is the longest country north-to-south in the world, extending across 39 degrees of latitude

facts.title: Geography of Chile
facts.body: Chile is one of the countries along the Ring of Fire, which is a belt bordering the Pacific Ocean that contains about 75% of the world's volcanoes and up to 90% of the world's earthquakes

facts.title: Geography of Chile
facts.body: The Atacama Desert in the north of Chile is the driest desert in the world; Ojos del Salado (6,893 m) in the Atacama Desert is the highest active volcano in the world, Chile's tallest mountain, and the second-highest in the Western Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere; the volcano's small crater lake is the world's highest lake at 6,390 m

facts.title: Geography of Cameroon
facts.body: Sometimes referred to as the hinge of Africa because of its central location on the continent and its position at the west-south juncture of the Gulf of Guinea; areas of thermal springs and indications of current or prior volcanic activity; Mount Cameroon, the highest mountain in Sub-Saharan west Africa, is an active volcano

facts.title: Geography of China
facts.body: World's fourth largest country (after Russia, Canada, and the US) and largest country situated entirely in Asia; Mount Everest, on the border with Nepal, is the world's tallest peak above sea level

facts.title: Geography of China
facts.body: The largest cave chamber in the world is the Miao Room, in the Gebihe cave system at China's Ziyun Getu He Chuandong National Park, which encloses about 10.78 million cu m (380.7 million cu ft); the world's largest sinkhole is the Xiaoxhai Tiankeng sinkhole in Chongqing Municipality, which is 660 m deep, with a volume of 130 million cu m

facts.title: Geography of Colombia
facts.body: Only South American country with coastlines on both the North Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea

facts.title: Geography of Costa Rica
facts.body: Four volcanoes, two of them active, rise near the capital of San Jose in the center of the country; one of the volcanoes, Irazu, erupted destructively in 1963-65

facts.title: Geography of Cuba
facts.body: Largest country in Caribbean and westernmost island of the Greater Antilles

facts.title: Geography of Cape Verde
facts.body: Strategic location 500 km from west coast of Africa near major north-south sea routes; one of four North Atlantic archipelagos that make up Macaronesia; the others are Azores (Portugal), Canary Islands (Spain), and Madeira (Portugal)

facts.title: Geography of Cyprus
facts.body: The third largest island in the Mediterranean Sea (after Sicily and Sardinia)

facts.title: Geography of Czechia
facts.body: Landlocked; strategically located on some of oldest and most significant land routes in Europe; Moravian Gate is a traditional military corridor between the North European Plain and the Danube in central Europe

facts.title: Geography of Czechia
facts.body: The Hranice Abyss in Czechia is the world's deepest surveyed freshwater cave at 519 m (1,703 ft); its survey is not complete, and it may be up to 800-1,200 m (2,625-3,937 ft) deep

facts.title: Geography of Germany
facts.body: Strategic location on North European Plain and along the entrance to the Baltic Sea; most major rivers in Germany -- the Rhine, Weser, Oder, Elbe -- flow northward; the Danube, which originates in the Black Forest, flows eastward

facts.title: Geography of Djibouti
facts.body: Strategic location near world's busiest shipping lanes and close to Arabian oilfields; Lac Assal (Lake Assal) is the lowest point in Africa and the saltiest lake in the world

facts.title: Geography of Denmark
facts.body: Composed of the Jutland Peninsula and a group of more than 400 islands (Danish Archipelago); controls Danish Straits (Skagerrak and Kattegat) linking Baltic and North Seas; about one-quarter of the population lives in greater Copenhagen

facts.title: Geography of Dominica
facts.body: Known as "The Nature Island of the Caribbean" due to its lush and varied flora and fauna, which are protected by an extensive natural park system; the most mountainous of the Lesser Antilles, its volcanic peaks are cones of lava craters and include Boiling Lake, the second-largest thermally active lake in the world

facts.title: Geography of Dominican Republic
facts.body: Shares island of Hispaniola with Haiti (eastern two-thirds makes up the Dominican Republic, western one-third is Haiti); the second largest country in the Antilles (after Cuba); geographically diverse with the Caribbean's tallest mountain, Pico Duarte, and lowest elevation and largest lake, Lago Enriquillo

facts.title: Geography of Algeria
facts.body: Largest country in Africa but 80% desert; canyons and caves in the southern Hoggar Mountains and in the barren Tassili n'Ajjer area in the southeast of the country contain numerous examples of prehistoric art -- rock paintings and carvings depicting human activities and wild and domestic animals (elephants, giraffes, cattle) -- that date to the African Humid Period, roughly 5,000 to 11,000 years ago, when the region was completely vegetated

facts.title: Geography of Estonia
facts.body: The mainland terrain is flat, boggy, and partly wooded; over 1,500 islands lie offshore

facts.title: Geography of Egypt
facts.body: Controls Sinai Peninsula, the only land bridge between Africa and remainder of Eastern Hemisphere; controls Suez Canal, a sea link between Indian Ocean and Mediterranean Sea

facts.title: Geography of Eritrea
facts.body: Strategic geopolitical position along world's busiest shipping lanes

facts.title: Geography of Spain
facts.body: Strategic location along approaches to Strait of Gibraltar; Spain controls a number of territories in northern Morocco, including the enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla and the islands of Penon de Velez de la Gomera, Penon de Alhucemas, and Islas Chafarinas; Spain's Canary Islands are one of four North Atlantic archipelagos that make up Macaronesia; the others are the Azores (Portugal), Madeira (Portugal), and Cabo Verde

facts.title: Geography of Ethiopia
facts.body: The most populous landlocked country in the world; the Blue Nile, the chief headstream of the Nile by water volume, rises in T'ana Hayk (Lake Tana) in northwest Ethiopia

facts.title: Geography of Finland
facts.body: Long boundary with Russia; Helsinki is northernmost national capital on European continent; population concentrated on small southwestern coastal plain

facts.title: Geography of Fiji
facts.body: Consists of 332 islands, approximately 110 of which are inhabited, and more than 500 islets

facts.title: Geography of France
facts.body: Largest Western European nation; most major French rivers -- the Meuse, Seine, Loire, Charente, Dordogne, and Garonne -- flow northward or westward into the Atlantic Ocean, only the Rhone flows southward into the Mediterranean Sea

facts.title: Geography of Gabon
facts.body: The country has maintained its pristine rain forest and rich biodiversity

facts.title: Geography of United Kingdom
facts.body: Lies near vital North Atlantic sea lanes; only 35 km (22 mi) from France and linked by tunnel under the English Channel (the Channel Tunnel or Chunnel); because of heavily indented coastline, no location is more than 125 km (78 mi) from tidal waters

facts.title: Geography of Georgia
facts.body: Strategically located east of the Black Sea, Georgia controls much of the Caucasus Mountains and the routes through them

facts.title: Geography of Georgia
facts.body: The world's four deepest caves are all in Georgia, including two that are the only known caves on earth deeper than 2,000 m: Krubera Cave at -2,197 m (-7,208 ft; reached in 2012) and Veryovkina Cave at -2,212 (-7,257 ft; reached in 2018)

facts.title: Geography of Ghana
facts.body: Lake Volta is the world's largest artificial lake (manmade reservoir) by surface area (8,482 sq km; 3,275 sq mi); the lake was created after the Akosombo Dam was completed in 1965

facts.title: Geography of Gambia
facts.body: Almost an enclave of Senegal; smallest country on the African mainland

facts.title: Geography of Guinea
facts.body: The Niger and its important tributary, the Milo River, have their sources in the Guinean highlands

facts.title: Geography of Equatorial Guinea
facts.body: Insular and continental regions widely separated; despite its name, no part of the equator passes through Equatorial Guinea -- the mainland part of the country is located just north of the equator

facts.title: Geography of Greece
facts.body: Strategic location dominating the Aegean Sea and southern approach to Turkish Straits; a peninsular country, with an archipelago of about 2,000 islands

facts.title: Geography of Guatemala
facts.body: Despite having both eastern and western coastlines (Caribbean Sea and Pacific Ocean), there are no natural harbors on the west coast

facts.title: Geography of Guatemala
facts.body: Guatemala is one of the countries along the Ring of Fire, which is a belt bordering the Pacific Ocean that contains about 75% of the world's volcanoes and up to 90% of the world's earthquakes

facts.title: Geography of Guinea-Bissau
facts.body: This small country is swampy along its western coast and is low-lying inland

facts.title: Geography of Guyana
