facts.body: The third-smallest country in South America after Suriname and Uruguay; contains some of the largest unspoiled rainforests on the continent

facts.title: Geography of Honduras
facts.body: Has only a short Pacific coast but a long Caribbean shoreline, including the virtually uninhabited eastern Mosquito Coast

facts.title: Geography of Croatia
facts.body: Controls most land routes from Western Europe to the Aegean Sea and Turkish Straits; most Adriatic Sea islands lie off the coast of Croatia -- some 1,200 islands, islets, ridges, and rocks

facts.title: Geography of Haiti
facts.body: Shares island of Hispaniola with Dominican Republic (western one-third is Haiti, eastern two-thirds is the Dominican Republic); it is the most mountainous nation in the Caribbean

facts.title: Geography of Hungary
facts.body: Landlocked; strategic location on main land routes between Western Europe and Balkan Peninsula, as well as between Ukraine and the Mediterranean basin; the Duna (Danube) and Tisza Rivers divide the country into three large regions

facts.title: Geography of Indonesia
facts.body: 13,466 islands are in the archipelago, of which 922 are permanently inhabited; Indonesia is the world's largest country composed solely of islands; the country straddles the equator and occupies a strategic location along major sea lanes from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific Ocean

facts.title: Geography of Indonesia
facts.body: Indonesia is one of the countries along the Ring of Fire, which is a belt bordering the Pacific Ocean that contains about 75% of the world's volcanoes, up to 90% of the world's earthquakes, and 80% of tsunamis

facts.title: Geography of Indonesia
facts.body: Despite having the fourth largest population in the world, Indonesia is the most heavily forested region on earth after the Amazon

facts.title: Geography of Ireland
facts.body: Strategic location on major air and sea routes between North America and northern Europe; over 40% of the population resides within 100 km of Dublin

facts.title: Geography of Israel
facts.body: Lake Tiberias (Sea of Galilee) is an important freshwater source; the Dead Sea is the second saltiest body of water in the world (after Lake Assal in Djibouti)

facts.title: Geography of Israel
facts.body: The Malham Cave in Mount Sodom is the world's longest salt cave at 10 km (6 mi); Mount Sodom is a hill about 220 m (722 ft) high that is 80% salt, with multiple salt layers covered by a veneer of rock

facts.title: Geography of India
facts.body: Dominates South Asian subcontinent; near important Indian Ocean trade routes; Kanchenjunga, third tallest mountain in the world, lies on the border with Nepal

facts.title: Geography of Iraq
facts.body: Strategic location on Shatt al Arab waterway and at the head of the Persian Gulf

facts.title: Geography of Iceland
facts.body: Strategic location between Greenland and Europe; westernmost European country; Reykjavik is the northernmost national capital in the world; more land covered by glaciers than in all of continental Europe

facts.title: Geography of Italy
facts.body: Strategic location dominating central Mediterranean, as well as southern sea and air approaches to Western Europe

facts.title: Geography of Jamaica
facts.body: Third largest island in the Caribbean (after Cuba and Hispaniola); strategic location between Cayman Trench and Jamaica Channel, the main sea lanes for the Panama Canal

facts.title: Geography of Jordan
facts.body: Strategic location at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba; the Arab country that shares the longest border with Israel and the West Bank; the Dead Sea, the lowest point in Asia and the second saltiest body of water in the world (after Lac Assal in Djibouti), lies on Jordan's western border with Israel and the West Bank; Jordan is almost landlocked but does have a 26 km southwestern coastline with a single port, Al 'Aqabah (Aqaba)

facts.title: Geography of Japan
facts.body: Strategic location in northeast Asia; composed of four main islands (the "Home Islands") -- Hokkaido, Honshu (the largest, most populous, and site of Tokyo, the capital), Shikoku, and Kyushu

facts.title: Geography of Japan
facts.body: A 2023 Geospatial Information Authority of Japan survey detected 100,000 islands and islets, but only the 14,125 islands with a circumference of at least 100 m (330 ft) were officially counted; about 260 of the islands are inhabited

facts.title: Geography of Japan
facts.body: Japan annually records the most earthquakes in the world; it is one of the countries along the Ring of Fire, which is a belt bordering the Pacific Ocean that contains about 75% of the world's volcanoes and up to 90% of the world's earthquakes

facts.title: Geography of Kenya
facts.body: The Kenyan Highlands comprise one of the most successful agricultural production regions in Africa; glaciers are found on Mount Kenya, Africa's second-highest peak; unique physiography supports abundant and varied wildlife of scientific and economic value; Lake Victoria, the world's largest tropical lake and the second-largest freshwater lake, is shared among three countries: Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda

facts.title: Geography of Kyrgyzstan
facts.body: Landlocked; entirely mountainous, dominated by the Tien Shan range; 94% of the country is 1,000 m above sea level with an average elevation of 2,750 m; many tall peaks, glaciers, and high-altitude lakes

facts.title: Geography of Cambodia
facts.body: A land of paddies and forests dominated by the Mekong River and Tonle Sap (Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake)

facts.title: Geography of Kiribati
facts.body: 21 of the 33 islands are inhabited; Banaba (Ocean Island) in Kiribati is one of the three great phosphate rock islands in the Pacific Ocean -- the others are Makatea in French Polynesia, and Nauru; Kiribati is the only country in the world to fall into all four hemispheres (northern, southern, eastern, and western)

facts.title: Geography of Comoros
facts.body: Important location at northern end of Mozambique Channel; the only Arab League country that lies entirely in the Southern Hemisphere

facts.title: Geography of Saint Kitts and Nevis
facts.body: Smallest country in the Western Hemisphere in terms of both area and population; the two volcanic islands are separated by a 3-km-wide (9-mi-wide) channel called The Narrows; on the southern tip of baseball-bat-shaped Saint Kitts lies the Great Salt Pond; Nevis Peak sits in the center of its ball-shaped namesake island

facts.title: Geography of North Korea
facts.body: Strategic location bordering China, South Korea, and Russia; mountainous interior is isolated and sparsely populated

facts.title: Geography of South Korea
facts.body: Strategic location on Korea Strait; about 3,000 mostly small and uninhabited islands lie off the western and southern coasts

facts.title: Geography of Kazakhstan
facts.body: World's largest landlocked country and one of only two landlocked countries in the world that extends into two continents (the other is Azerbaijan); Russia leases approximately 6,000 sq km (2,317 sq mi) of territory enclosing the Baikonur Cosmodrome

facts.title: Geography of Laos
facts.body: Landlocked; most of the country is mountainous and thickly forested; the Mekong River forms a large part of the western boundary with Thailand

facts.title: Geography of Lebanon
facts.body: Smallest country in continental Asia; Nahr el Litani is the only major river in Near East not crossing an international boundary

facts.title: Geography of Saint Lucia
facts.body: The twin Pitons (Gros Piton and Petit Piton), striking cone-shaped peaks south of Soufrière, are one of the scenic natural highlights of the Caribbean

facts.title: Geography of Liechtenstein
facts.body: Along with Uzbekistan, one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world; variety of microclimatic variations based on elevation

facts.title: Geography of Sri Lanka
facts.body: Strategic location near major Indian Ocean sea lanes; Adam's Bridge is a chain of limestone shoals between the southeastern coast of India and the northwestern coast of Sri Lanka; geological evidence suggests that this 50-km (31-mi) bridge once connected India and Sri Lanka; ancient records seem to indicate that a foot passage was possible between the two land masses until the 15th century, when the land bridge broke up in a cyclone

facts.title: Geography of Liberia
facts.body: Facing the Atlantic Ocean, the coastline is characterized by lagoons, mangrove swamps, and river-deposited sandbars; the inland grassy plateau supports limited agriculture

facts.title: Geography of Lesotho
facts.body: Landlocked, surrounded by South Africa; mountainous, more than 80% of the country is 1,800 m (5,900 ft) above sea level

facts.title: Geography of Lithuania
facts.body: Fertile central plains are separated by hilly uplands that are ancient glacial deposits

facts.title: Geography of Latvia
facts.body: Most of the country is composed of fertile low-lying plains with some hills in the east

facts.title: Geography of Libya
facts.body: The volcano Waw an Namus lies in south central Libya in the middle of the Sahara; the caldera is an oasis -- the name means "oasis of mosquitoes" -- containing several small lakes that host many species of insects and birds

facts.title: Geography of Morocco
facts.body: Strategic location along Strait of Gibraltar; the only African nation to have both Atlantic and Mediterranean coastlines; the waters off the Atlantic coast are particularly rich fishing areas

facts.title: Geography of Monaco
facts.body: Second-smallest independent state in the world (after the Holy See); smallest country with a coastline; almost entirely urban

facts.title: Geography of Moldova
facts.body: Landlocked; has many types of sedimentary rocks and minerals, including sand, gravel, gypsum, and limestone

facts.title: Geography of Madagascar
facts.body: World's fourth-largest island; strategic location along Mozambique Channel; despite Madagascar’s close proximity to the African continent, ocean currents isolate the island, resulting in high rates of endemic plant and animal species; approximately 90% of the flora and fauna on the island are found nowhere else

facts.title: Geography of Marshall Islands
facts.body: Kwajalein atoll surrounds the world's largest lagoon; the island city of Ebeye is the second largest settlement in the Marshall Islands, after the capital of Majuro, and one of the most densely populated locations in the Pacific

facts.title: Geography of North Macedonia
facts.body: Landlocked; major transportation corridor from Western and Central Europe to Aegean Sea and Southern Europe to Western Europe

facts.title: Geography of Mali
facts.body: Landlocked; divided into three natural zones: the southern, cultivated Sudanese; the central, semiarid Sahelian; and the northern, arid Saharan

facts.title: Geography of Myanmar
facts.body: Strategic location near major Indian Ocean shipping lanes; the north-south flowing Irrawaddy River is the country's largest and most important commercial waterway

facts.title: Geography of Mauritania
facts.body: Mauritania is considered part of both North Africa's Maghreb region and West Africa's Sahel region; most of the population is concentrated in the cities of Nouakchott and Nouadhibou and along the Senegal River in the southern part of the country

facts.title: Geography of Malta
facts.body: The country is an archipelago, with only the three largest islands (Malta, Ghawdex or Gozo, and Kemmuna or Comino) inhabited; numerous bays provide good harbors

facts.title: Geography of Mauritius
facts.body: The main island, from which the country derives its name, is of volcanic origin and is almost entirely surrounded by coral reefs; former home of the extinct dodo, a large flightless bird related to pigeons

facts.title: Geography of Maldives
facts.body: Smallest Asian country; archipelago of 1,190 coral islands grouped into 26 atolls (200 inhabited islands, plus 80 islands with tourist resorts); strategic location along major sea lanes in Indian Ocean

facts.title: Geography of Malawi
facts.body: Landlocked; Lake Nyasa, about 580 km (360 mi) long, is the country's most prominent physical feature; it contains more fish species than any other lake on earth

facts.title: Geography of Mexico
facts.body: Strategic location on southern border of the US; Mexico is one of the countries along the Ring of Fire, which is a belt bordering the Pacific Ocean that contains about 75% of the world's volcanoes and up to 90% of the world's earthquakes

facts.title: Geography of Mexico
facts.body: The Sac Actun cave system at 348 km (216 mi) is the longest underwater cave in the world and the second longest cave worldwide, after Mammoth Cave in the United States (see "Geography - note" under United States)

facts.title: Geography of Mexico
facts.body: The prominent Yucatán Peninsula that divides the Gulf of America from the Caribbean Sea is shared by Mexico, Guatemala, and Belize; on the northern coast of Yucatan near the town of Chicxulub lie the remnants of a massive asteroid or comet crater about 150 km (93 mi) in diameter and extending into the Gulf of America; the impact is believed to have initiated a worldwide climate disruption that caused a mass extinction of 75% of the earth's plant and animal species, including the non-avian dinosaurs

facts.title: Geography of Malaysia
facts.body: Strategic location along Strait of Malacca and southern South China Sea

facts.title: Geography of Mozambique
facts.body: The Zambezi River flows through the north-central and most fertile part of the country

facts.title: Geography of Namibia
facts.body: The Namib Desert, after which the country is named, is considered to be the oldest desert in the world; some 14% of the land is protected, including virtually the entire Namib Desert coastal strip

facts.title: Geography of Niger
facts.body: Landlocked; one of the hottest countries in the world; northern four-fifths is desert, southern one-fifth is savanna that is suitable for livestock and limited agriculture

facts.title: Geography of Nigeria
facts.body: The Niger River enters the country in the northwest and flows southward through tropical rainforests and swamps to its delta in the Gulf of Guinea

facts.title: Geography of Nicaragua
facts.body: Largest country in Central America; contains the largest freshwater body in Central America, Lago de Nicaragua

facts.title: Geography of Netherlands
facts.body: Located at mouths of three major European rivers (Rhine (Rijn), Meuse (Maas), and Scheldt (Schelde)); about a quarter of the country lies below sea level and only about half of the land exceeds one meter above sea level

facts.title: Geography of Norway
facts.body: About two-thirds mountains; some 50,000 islands off its much-indented coastline; strategic location adjacent to sea lanes and air routes in North Atlantic; one of the most rugged and longest coastlines in the world

facts.title: Geography of Nepal
facts.body: Landlocked; strategic location between China and India; contains eight of world's 10 highest peaks, including Mount Everest and Kanchenjunga -- the world's tallest and third-tallest mountains -- on the borders with China and India, respectively

facts.title: Geography of Nauru
facts.body: Nauru is the third-smallest country in the world behind the Holy See (Vatican City) and Monaco; it is the smallest country in the Pacific Ocean, the smallest country outside Europe, the world's smallest island country, and the world's smallest independent republic; situated just 53 km south of the equator, Nauru is one of the three great phosphate rock islands in the Pacific Ocean -- the others are Banaba (Ocean Island) in Kiribati and Makatea in French Polynesia

facts.title: Geography of New Zealand
facts.body: Consists of two main islands and a number of smaller islands; South Island, the larger main island, is the 12th-largest island in the world and is divided along its length by the Southern Alps; North Island is the 14th-largest island in the world and is not as mountainous, but it is marked by volcanism

facts.title: Geography of New Zealand
facts.body: New Zealand lies along the Ring of Fire, which is a belt bordering the Pacific Ocean that contains about 75% of the world's volcanoes and up to 90% of the world's earthquakes

facts.title: Geography of New Zealand
facts.body: Almost 90% of the population lives in cities and over three-quarters on North Island; Wellington is the southernmost national capital in the world

facts.title: Geography of Oman
facts.body: Consists of Oman proper and two northern exclaves, Musandam and Al Madhah; the former is a peninsula that occupies a strategic location adjacent to the Strait of Hormuz

facts.title: Geography of Panama
facts.body: Strategic location on eastern end of isthmus forming land bridge that connects North and South America; controls the Panama Canal, which links the North Atlantic Ocean with the North Pacific Ocean via the Caribbean Sea

facts.title: Geography of Peru
facts.body: Shares control of Lago Titicaca, world's highest navigable lake, with Bolivia; a remote slope of Nevado Mismi, a 5,316-m (17,441-ft) peak, is the ultimate source of the Amazon River

facts.title: Geography of Peru
facts.body: Peru is one of the countries along the Ring of Fire, which is a belt bordering the Pacific Ocean that contains about 75% of the world's volcanoes and up to 90% of the world's earthquakes

facts.title: Geography of Peru
facts.body: On 19 February 1600, Mount Huaynaputina in the southern Peruvian Andes erupted in the largest volcanic explosion in South America in historical times; intermittent eruptions lasted until 5 March 1600 and pumped an estimated 16 to 32 million metric tons of particulates into the atmosphere, reducing the amount of sunlight reaching the earth's surface and affecting weather worldwide; over the next two-and-a-half years, millions died around the globe in famines from bitterly cold winters, cool summers, and the loss of crops and animals

facts.title: Geography of Papua New Guinea
facts.body: Shares island of New Guinea with Indonesia; highlands that trend from east to west break up New Guinea into diverse ecoregions; one of world's largest swamps lies along the southwest coast

facts.title: Geography of Papua New Guinea
facts.body: Papua New Guinea is one of the countries along the Ring of Fire, which is a belt bordering the Pacific Ocean that contains about 75% of the world's volcanoes and up to 90% of the world's earthquakes

facts.title: Geography of Philippines
facts.body: For decades, the Philippine archipelago was reported as having 7,107 islands; in 2016, the national mapping authority reported that hundreds of new islands had been discovered and increased the number of islands to 7,641, though not all of the new islands have been verified

facts.title: Geography of Philippines
facts.body: The Philippines is one of the countries along the Ring of Fire, which is a belt bordering the Pacific Ocean that contains about 75% of the world's volcanoes and up to 90% of the world's earthquakes

facts.title: Geography of Philippines
facts.body: The Philippines sits on the Pacific typhoon belt, and an average of 9 typhoons make landfall on the islands each year, with about 5 being destructive; the country is the most exposed in the world to tropical storms

facts.title: Geography of Pakistan
facts.body: Controls Khyber Pass and Bolan Pass, traditional invasion routes between Central Asia and India

facts.title: Geography of Poland
facts.body: Historically an area of conflict because of flat terrain and the lack of natural barriers on the North European Plain

facts.title: Geography of Palestine
facts.body: Landlocked; highlands are main recharge area for Israel's coastal aquifers (2017)

facts.title: Geography of Portugal
facts.body: Azores and Madeira Islands occupy strategic locations along western sea approaches to Strait of Gibraltar; they are two of the four North Atlantic archipelagos that make up Macaronesia; the others are the Canary Islands (Spain) and Cabo Verde

facts.title: Geography of Palau
facts.body: Westernmost archipelago in the Caroline chain, consists of six island groups totaling more than 300 islands; includes world-famous Rock Islands

facts.title: Geography of Paraguay
facts.body: Landlocked; lies between Argentina, Bolivia, and Brazil; population concentrated in eastern and southern part of country

facts.title: Geography of Qatar
facts.body: The peninsula occupies a strategic location in the central Persian Gulf near major petroleum deposits

facts.title: Geography of Romania
facts.body: Controls the most easily traversable land route between the Balkans, Moldova, and Ukraine; the Carpathian Mountains dominate the center of the country, and the Danube River forms much of the southern boundary with Serbia and Bulgaria

facts.title: Geography of Serbia
facts.body: Landlocked; controls one of the major land routes from Western Europe to Turkey and the Near East

facts.title: Geography of Russia
facts.body: Largest country in the world in terms of area; despite its size, much of the country lacks the soil and climate (either too cold or too dry) for agriculture

facts.title: Geography of Russia
facts.body: Russia's far east, particularly the Kamchatka Peninsula, lies along the Ring of Fire, which is a belt bordering the Pacific Ocean that contains about 75% of the world's volcanoes and up to 90% of the world's earthquakes

facts.title: Geography of Russia
facts.body: Mount El'brus is Europe's tallest peak; Lake Baikal, the deepest lake in the world, is estimated to hold one fifth of the world's fresh surface water

facts.title: Geography of Russia
facts.body: Kaliningrad oblast is an exclave annexed from Germany after World War II; its capital city of Kaliningrad -- formerly Koenigsberg -- is the only Baltic port in Russia that remains ice-free in the winter

facts.title: Geography of Rwanda
facts.body: Landlocked; most of the country is intensively cultivated and rugged, with the population predominantly rural

facts.title: Geography of Saudi Arabia
facts.body: Saudi Arabia is the largest country in the world without a river; extensive coastlines on the Persian Gulf and Red Sea allow for considerable shipping (especially of crude oil) through the Persian Gulf and Suez Canal

facts.title: Geography of Solomon Islands
facts.body: Strategic location on sea routes between the South Pacific Ocean, the Solomon Sea, and the Coral Sea; Rennell Island, the southernmost in the Solomon Islands chain, is one of the world’s largest raised coral atolls; the island’s Lake Tegano, formerly a lagoon on the atoll, is the largest lake in the insular Pacific (15,500 hectares; 38,300 acres)

facts.title: Geography of Seychelles
facts.body: The smallest African country in terms of both area and population; the constitution of the Republic of Seychelles lists 155 islands, including 42 granitic and 113 coralline; the largest island by far is Mahe, which is home to about 90% of the population and is the site of the capital city of Victoria

facts.title: Geography of Sudan
facts.body: The Nile is Sudan's primary water source; its major tributaries, the White Nile and the Blue Nile, meet at Khartoum to form the River Nile, which flows northward through Egypt to the Mediterranean Sea

facts.title: Geography of Sweden
facts.body: Strategic location along Danish Straits linking Baltic and North Seas; Sweden has almost 100,000 lakes, the largest of which, Vanern, is the third-largest in Europe

facts.title: Geography of Singapore
facts.body: Focal point for Southeast Asian sea routes; consists of about 60 islands, the largest of which by far is Pulau Ujong; land reclamation has removed many former islands and created a number of new ones

facts.title: Geography of Slovenia
facts.body: Despite its small size, this eastern Alpine country controls some of Europe's major transit routes

facts.title: Geography of Slovakia
facts.body: Landlocked; most of the country is rugged and mountainous; the Tatra Mountains in the north are interspersed with many scenic lakes and valleys

facts.title: Geography of Sierra Leone
facts.body: Rainfall along the coast can reach 495 cm (195 in) a year, making it one of the wettest places along coastal western Africa

facts.title: Geography of San Marino
facts.body: Landlocked; an enclave of (completely surrounded by) Italy; smallest independent state in Europe after the Holy See and Monaco; dominated by the Apennine Mountains

facts.title: Geography of Senegal
facts.body: Westernmost country on the African continent; The Gambia is almost an enclave within Senegal

facts.title: Geography of Somalia
facts.body: Strategic location on Horn of Africa along southern approaches to Bab el Mandeb and route through Red Sea and Suez Canal

facts.title: Geography of Suriname
facts.body: Smallest independent country on the South American continent; mostly tropical rainforest; great diversity of flora and fauna; relatively small population, mostly along the coast

facts.title: Geography of South Sudan
facts.body: Landlocked; The Sudd is a vast swamp in the north central region of South Sudan, formed by the White Nile; its size is variable but can reach some 15% of the country's total area during the rainy season; it is one of the world's largest wetlands

facts.title: Geography of São Tomé and Príncipe
facts.body: The second-smallest African country (after the Seychelles); the two main islands form part of a chain of extinct volcanoes, and both are mountainous

facts.title: Geography of El Salvador
facts.body: Smallest Central American country and only one without a coastline on the Caribbean Sea

facts.title: Geography of Syria
facts.body: The capital of Damascus is located at an oasis fed by the Barada River and is thought to be one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities; there are Israeli settlements and civilian land-use sites in the Israeli-controlled Golan Heights (2017)

facts.title: Geography of Chad
facts.body: A wide variety of animals lived in modern-day Chad during the African Humid Period, including elephants, giraffes, hippos, and antelope; the last remnant of this "Green Sahara" exists in the Lakes of Ounianga in northern Chad, a series of 18 interconnected freshwater, saline, and hypersaline lakes

facts.title: Geography of Chad
facts.body: Lake Chad, the most significant water body in the Sahel, is a remnant of a former inland sea, paleolake Mega-Chad; at its greatest extent, sometime before 5000 B.C., Lake Mega-Chad was the largest of four Saharan paleolakes that existed during the African Humid Period; it covered an area of about 400,000 sq km (150,000 sq mi), roughly the size of today's Caspian Sea

facts.title: Geography of Togo
facts.body: Stretches through six distinct geographic regions; climate varies from tropical to savanna

facts.title: Geography of Tajikistan
facts.body: Landlocked; highest point, Qullai Ismoili Somoni (formerly Communism Peak), was the tallest mountain in the former USSR

facts.title: Geography of Timor-Leste
facts.body: The island of Timor is part of the Malay Archipelago and is the largest and easternmost of the Lesser Sunda Islands; the district of Oecussi is an exclave separated from Timor-Leste proper by Indonesia; Timor-Leste is the only Asian country located completely in the Southern Hemisphere

facts.title: Geography of Turkmenistan
facts.body: Landlocked; the western and central low-lying desolate portions of the country make up the great Garagum (Kara-Kum) desert, which occupies over 80% of the country; eastern part is plateau

facts.title: Geography of Tonga
facts.body: The western islands (making up the Tongan Volcanic Arch) are all of volcanic origin; the eastern islands are nonvolcanic and are composed of coral limestone and sand

facts.title: Geography of Türkiye
facts.body: Strategic location controlling the Turkish Straits (Bosporus, Sea of Marmara, Dardanelles) that link the Black and Aegean Seas; the 3% of Turkish territory north of the Straits lies in Europe and goes by the names of European Turkey, Eastern Thrace, or Turkish Thrace; the 97% of the country in Asia is referred to as Anatolia; Istanbul, which straddles the Bosporus, is the only metropolis in the world located on two continents; Mount Ararat, reputed to be the landing place of Noah's ark, is in the far-eastern part of the country

facts.title: Geography of Trinidad and Tobago
facts.body: Pitch Lake, on Trinidad's southwestern coast, is the world's largest natural reservoir of asphalt

facts.title: Geography of Tuvalu
facts.body: One of the smallest and most remote countries on earth; six of the nine coral atolls -- Nanumea, Nui, Vaitupu, Nukufetau, Funafuti, and Nukulaelae -- have lagoons open to the ocean; Nanumaya and Niutao have landlocked lagoons; Niulakita does not have a lagoon

facts.title: Geography of Tanzania
facts.body: Kilimanjaro is the highest point in Africa and one of only three mountain ranges on the continent that has glaciers (the others are Mount Kenya in Kenya and the Ruwenzori Mountains on the Uganda-Democratic Republic of the Congo border); Tanzania is bordered by three of the largest lakes on the continent: Lake Victoria (the world's second-largest freshwater lake) in the north, Lake Tanganyika (the world's second-deepest) in the west, and Lake Nyasa (Lake Malawi) in the southwest

facts.title: Geography of Ukraine
facts.body: Strategic position at the crossroads between Europe and Asia; second-largest country in Europe after Russia

facts.title: Geography of Uganda
facts.body: Landlocked; fertile, well-watered country with many lakes and rivers; Lake Victoria, the world's largest tropical lake and second-largest freshwater lake, is shared among three countries: Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda

facts.title: Geography of United States
facts.body: World's third-largest country by size (after Russia and Canada) and by population (after China and India); Mt. McKinley is the highest point (6,190 m; 20,308 ft) in North America, and Death Valley is the lowest point (-86 m; -282 ft)

facts.title: Geography of United States
facts.body: The western US coast and the southern coast of Alaska lie along the Ring of Fire, which is a belt bordering the Pacific Ocean that contains about 75% of the world's volcanoes and up to 90% of the world's earthquakes

facts.title: Geography of United States
facts.body: The Aleutian Islands are a chain of volcanic islands that divide the Bering Sea (north) from the main Pacific Ocean (south); they extend about 1,800 km (1,118 mi) westward from the Alaskan Peninsula; the archipelago consists of 14 larger islands, 55 smaller islands, and hundreds of islets; there are 41 active volcanoes on the islands, which together form a large northern section of the Ring of Fire

facts.title: Geography of United States
facts.body: Mammoth Cave, in west-central Kentucky, is the world's longest known cave system with more than 650 km (405 miles) of surveyed passageways, which is nearly twice as long as the second-longest cave system, the Sac Actun underwater cave in Mexico (see "Geography - note" under Mexico)

facts.title: Geography of United States
facts.body: Kazumura Cave on the island of Hawaii is the world's longest and deepest lava-tube cave; it has been surveyed at 66 km (41 mi) long and 1,102 m (3,614 ft) deep

facts.title: Geography of United States
facts.body: Bracken Cave outside San Antonio, Texas is the world's largest bat cave and the summer home to the largest colony of bats in the world; an estimated 20 million Mexican free-tailed bats roost in the cave from March to October, making it the world's largest known concentration of mammals

facts.title: Geography of Uruguay
facts.body: Second-smallest South American country (after Suriname); most of the low-lying landscape (three-quarters of the country) is grassland, ideal for cattle and sheep

facts.title: Geography of Uzbekistan
facts.body: Along with Liechtenstein, one of the only two doubly landlocked countries in the world

facts.title: Geography of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
facts.body: The administration of the islands of the Grenadines group is divided between Saint Vincent and the Grenadines and Grenada; Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is composed of 32 islands and cays

facts.title: Geography of Venezuela
facts.body: The country lies on major sea and air routes linking North and South America

facts.title: Geography of Venezuela
facts.body: Venezuela has some of the most unique geology in the world; tepuis are the massive table-top mountains of the western Guiana Highlands that tend to be isolated and thus support unique endemic plant and animal species; their sheer cliffsides help create some of the most spectacular waterfalls in the world, including Angel Falls, the world's highest (979 m; 3,212 ft) that drops from Auyan Tepui

facts.title: Geography of Vietnam
facts.body: Extending 1,650 km (1,025 mi) north to south, the country is only 50 km (31 mi) across at its narrowest point

facts.title: Geography of Vietnam
facts.body: Son Doong in Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park is the world's largest cave (greatest cross-sectional area) and is the largest known cave passage in the world by volume at 38.5 million cu m (about 1.35 billion cu ft); it connects to Thoong cave, but not yet officially -- when recognized, it will add an additional 1.6 million cu m; it is so massive that it contains its own jungle, underground river, and localized weather system, with clouds forming inside the cave and spewing from its exits

facts.title: Geography of Vanuatu
facts.body: A Y-shaped chain of four main islands and 80 smaller islands; several of the islands have active volcanoes, including several underwater volcanoes

facts.title: Geography of Yemen
facts.body: Strategic location on Bab el Mandeb, the strait linking the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden and one of world's most active shipping lanes

facts.title: Geography of South Africa
facts.body: South Africa completely surrounds Lesotho and almost completely surrounds Eswatini

facts.title: Geography of South Africa
facts.body: Sometimes mistaken for the southernmost point of Africa, the Cape of Good Hope is more accurately described as the southwestern-most point of the African continent; Cape Agulhas, the meeting point of the Atlantic and Indian Oceans, is the southernmost point of the African continent

facts.title: Geography of Zambia
facts.body: Landlocked; the Zambezi forms a natural river boundary with Zimbabwe; Lake Kariba on the Zambia-Zimbabwe border forms the world's largest reservoir by volume (180 cu km; 43 cu mi)

facts.title: Geography of Zimbabwe
facts.body: Landlocked; the Zambezi forms a natural river boundary with Zambia; in full flood (February-April), the massive Victoria Falls on the river forms the world's largest curtain of falling water; Lake Kariba on the Zambia-Zimbabwe border forms the world's largest reservoir by volume (180 cu km; 43 cu mi)

facts.title: A whole country above 1,000 metres
facts.body: Every part of Lesotho lies more than 1,000 metres above sea level. It is also completely surrounded by South Africa; its capital, Maseru, sits right at that border.

facts.title: A mountain with most of itself below the surface
facts.body: Measured from its underwater base to its summit, Hawaii’s Mauna Kea rises more than 10,210 metres. “Tallest from base” and “highest above sea level” are different records.

facts.title: Why it is called Andorra
facts.body: The origin of the country's name is obscure; may originate from the Navarrese word andurrial, meaning "shrub-covered land;" alternatively, may derive from the Arabic ad-darra meaning "the forest," a reference to its location; many other theories exist

facts.title: Why it is called United Arab Emirates
facts.body: Self-descriptive country name; the name Arabia can be traced back at least as far as the ancient Egyptians, who referred to the region as "Ar Rabi;" "emirates" derives from amir , the Arabic word for "commander," "lord," or "prince;" the former name, Trucial States, refers to a maritime truce from 1820 between the British and the Arab sheikhdoms

facts.title: Why it is called Afghanistan
facts.body: The name "Afghan" originally referred to the Pashtun people, but today it is understood to include all the country's ethnic groups; the suffix "-stan" means "place of" or "country," so Afghanistan literally means the "Land of the Afghans"

facts.title: Why it is called Antigua and Barbuda
facts.body: Antiguo is Spanish for "ancient" or "old;" Christopher COLUMBUS named the island in 1493, after the church of Santa Maria la Antigua (Old Saint Mary's) in Seville, Spain; barbuda is Spanish for "bearded" and may refer to the island's lichen-covered fig trees

facts.title: Why it is called Albania
facts.body: Name may be derived from the pre-Celtic word alb , meaning "hill," or from the Indo-European root word albh , meaning "white;" the local name "Shqiperia" is derived from the Albanian word shqiponje ("eagle") and is popularly interpreted to mean "Land of the Eagles"

facts.title: Why it is called Armenia
facts.body: The etymology of the country's name remains obscure; according to tradition, the local name for the country, Hayastan, comes from Hayk, the legendary patriarch of the Armenians and the great-great-grandson of Noah; the name Armenia was first recorded in a rock inscription from A.D. 521 in modern-day Iran

facts.title: Why it is called Angola
facts.body: In the 15th century, Portuguese explorers derived the name from the title "N'gola," which was held by kings of the Ndongo

facts.title: Why it is called Argentina
facts.body: The name is derived from one of the Spanish words for "silver," but the origin is unclear; it may have described the land next to the Rio de la Plata ("Silver River"), a major river that forms the boundary between Argentina and Uruguay; another possible source is the Spanish explorers in the 16th century mistakenly believing that the silver ornaments they bought from inhabitants came from a local source of silver

facts.title: Why it is called Austria
facts.body: The name Oesterreich means "eastern realm" and dates to the 10th century; the designation refers to the fact that Austria was the easternmost extension of Bavaria and the German peoples; the word Austria is a Latinization of the German name

facts.title: Why it is called Australia
facts.body: The name Australia derives from the Latin australis meaning "southern;" the Australian landmass was long referred to as "Terra Australis," or the Southern Land

facts.title: Why it is called Azerbaijan
facts.body: The name can be translated as "Fire Keeper" or "The Land of Fire," from the local word azer , or "fire," and baydjan , a word derived from the Iranian word baykan , or "guardian;" may refer to fire worshippers who lived in the region

facts.title: Why it is called Bosnia and Herzegovina
facts.body: The larger northern territory is named for the Bosna River; the smaller southern section takes its name from the Old Serbian word herceg , meaning "duke," combined with the possessive - ov and the suffix - ina , meaning "country," to denote "dukedom"

facts.title: Why it is called Barbados
facts.body: The name is the plural of the Spanish word barbado and means "the bearded ones," which could refer either to the beard-like leaves of the island's fig trees or to the beards of Carib inhabitants

facts.title: Why it is called Bangladesh
facts.body: The name is a compound of the Bengali words Bangla (Bengali) and desh (country)

facts.title: Why it is called Belgium
facts.body: The name derives from the Belgae, an ancient Celtic tribal confederation that inhabited an area between the English Channel and the west bank of the Rhine in the first centuries B.C.

facts.title: Why it is called Burkina Faso
facts.body: Name translates as "Land of the Worthy Men," from the Dyula words burkina , or "worthy," and faso , which means "land" or literally "father village," from fa , or "father," and so , or "village"

facts.title: Why it is called Bulgaria
facts.body: Named after the Bulgar tribes who settled the lower Balkan region in the 7th century A.D.; the tribal name may come from the Turkic word bulga , or "mixed," referring to the blend of Turkic and Slavic ethnicities in the tribes

facts.title: Why it is called Bahrain
facts.body: The name means "the two seas" in Arabic and refers to the water bodies on each side of the archipelago

facts.title: Why it is called Burundi
facts.body: Name dates from 1966 and is derived from the name of the local Bantu people, the Rundi or Barundi; ba - is the prefix for the people, and bu - is the prefix for the country; the former name, Urundi, is the Swahili version

facts.title: Why it is called Benin
facts.body: The current name comes from a local ethnic group, the Bini, whose name may be related to the Arabic word bani , meaning "sons;" the former name, Dahomey, comes from a previous kingdom in the area called Dan Homé

facts.title: Why it is called Brunei
facts.body: Derivation of the name is unclear; the name may come from the Sanskrit word bhumi , meaning "land" or "region"

facts.title: Why it is called Bolivia
facts.body: The country is named in honor of Simón BOLÍVAR, a 19th-century leader in the South American wars for independence

facts.title: Why it is called Brazil
facts.body: The country name derives from the brazil tree that used to grow plentifully along the coast of Brazil and that was used to produce a deep red dye

facts.title: Why it is called Bahamas
facts.body: Name may be derived from the Spanish baha mar , meaning "low sea," which describes the shallow waters of the Bahama Banks; alternatively, it may be a form of the local name Guanahani, which is of unknown origin and meaning

facts.title: Why it is called Bhutan
facts.body: Name may derive from the Sanskrit words bhoṭa , the name for Tibet, and anta , meaning "end" -- a reference to Bhutan's location at the southernmost end of Tibet; the local Dzongkha name Druk Yul means "Land of the Dragon"

facts.title: Why it is called Botswana
facts.body: The name Botswana means "Land of the Tswana," referring to the country's largest ethnic group

facts.title: Why it is called Belarus
facts.body: The name is a compound of the Slavic words "bel" (white) and "Rus" (the Old East Slavic ethnic designation) to form the meaning White Rusian or White Ruthenian

facts.title: Why it is called Belize
facts.body: Traditionally believed to be derived from the Spanish pronunciation of the last name of Scottish explorer Peter Wallace, who settled in the area in 1638; alternatively, may be named for the Belize River, whose name possibly derives from the Maya word "belix," meaning "muddy-watered"

facts.title: Why it is called Canada
facts.body: The name is probably derived from the Huron or Iroquois word kanata , meaning village or camp

facts.title: Why it is called Democratic Republic of the Congo
facts.body: Named for the Congo River, most of which lies within the DRC; the river name derives from Kongo, a Bantu kingdom in the area

facts.title: Why it is called Central African Republic
facts.body: Self-descriptive name specifying the country's location on the continent; "Africa" is derived from the Roman designation of the area corresponding to present-day Tunisia, "Africa terra," which meant "Land of the Afri" (the tribe resident in that area), but which eventually came to mean the entire continent

facts.title: Why it is called Republic of the Congo
facts.body: Named for the Congo River, which makes up much of the country's eastern border; the river name derives from Kongo, a Bantu kingdom in the area

facts.title: Why it is called Switzerland
facts.body: Name derives from the canton of Schwyz, one of the founding cantons of the Swiss Confederacy formed in the late 13th century

facts.title: Why it is called Côte d’Ivoire
facts.body: Name, which means "Ivory Coast" in French, reflects the ivory trade in the region from the 15th to 17th centuries; the French version of the name has been used internationally since 1986, at the country's request

facts.title: Why it is called Chile
facts.body: Derivation of the name is unclear; it may come from a local word meaning either "land's end" or "cold," or a local word that was confused with the Mexican Spanish word chili , meaning a chili pepper, in reference to the area's shape

facts.title: Why it is called Cameroon
facts.body: In the 16th century, Portuguese explorers named an estuary near the mouth of the Wouri River the Rio dos Camaroes (River of Prawns) after the abundant shrimp in the water; the name Camaroes evolved into "Cameroon"

facts.title: Why it is called China
facts.body: English name could be derived from the Qin (Chin, Ts'in) rulers in the 3rd century B.C., or from the province of Shaanxi (Shensi) with its capital of Xi'an (Sian); the Chinese name Zhongguo translates as "Central Nation" or "Middle Country"

facts.title: Why it is called Costa Rica
facts.body: The name means "rich coast" in Spanish; Christopher COLUMBUS named it in 1502, referring to the region's abundant vegetation and water

facts.title: Why it is called Cuba
facts.body: The origin of the name is disputed; it could be derived from a local Taino word, either cubao , meaning "where fertile land is abundant," or coabana, meaning "great place"

facts.title: Why it is called Cape Verde
facts.body: The name derives from the Cape Verde (Green Cape) peninsula on the Senegalese coast, the westernmost point of Africa and the nearest mainland to the islands

facts.title: Why it is called Cyprus
facts.body: The Greek name for the island is Kupros, which is probably derived from the Sumerian kabar , meaning "copper" or "bronze;" copper mines were located on the island in antiquity

facts.title: Why it is called Czechia
facts.body: Name derives from the Czechs, a West Slavic tribe who rose to prominence in the late 9th century A.D.; the tribal name is said to come from an ancestral chief

facts.title: Why it is called Germany
facts.body: The origin of the name is unclear; it may come from Celtic words meaning "neighboring people," or it may derive from Germanic words meaning either "spear man" or "head man;" the native designation "Deutsch" comes from the Old High German "diutisc" meaning "national"

facts.title: Why it is called Djibouti
facts.body: The country name derives from the capital city of Djibouti

facts.title: Why it is called Denmark
facts.body: The name derives from the words Dane , a tribal name with unclear Germanic origins, and mark , a Danish word that refers to a march (borderland)

facts.title: Why it is called Dominica
facts.body: The island was named by explorer Christopher COLUMBUS for the day of the week on which he spotted it, Sunday ( Domingo in Spanish, dominica dies in Latin), 3 November 1493

facts.title: Why it is called Dominican Republic
facts.body: The name is a latinized form of the Spanish term Santo Domingo , meaning "holy Sunday;" Spanish explorers originally settled the island on a Sunday in 1496, and the name was first given to the island of Hispaniola as a whole in 1697

facts.title: Why it is called Algeria
facts.body: The country name derives from the capital city of Algiers

facts.title: Why it is called Ecuador
facts.body: The name is the Spanish word for "equator," referring to its geographic position

facts.title: Why it is called Estonia
facts.body: Derives from the name of the people who lived along the eastern Baltic Sea in the first centuries A.D., which came from the Baltic word aueist , meaning "waterside dwellers"

facts.title: Why it is called Egypt
facts.body: The English name Egypt derives from the ancient Greek name for the country, "Aguptos," and the ancient Roman name, "Aegyptus," with the Greek form coming from the words aia gupos , or "land of the vulture;" the Arabic name for the country, Misr, can be traced to the Assyrian word misir , meaning "fort"

facts.title: Why it is called Eritrea
facts.body: The country name derives from the ancient Greek name Erythra Thalassa , meaning "Red Sea," the body of water that borders the country

facts.title: Why it is called Spain
facts.body: Derivation of the name España is uncertain; the Basque words ezpain or espan ("edge," as in a river bank) are possible sources, or the Punic word span , meaning "rabbit;" some academics tie it to the god Hesperus from Greco-Roman mythology

facts.title: Why it is called Ethiopia
facts.body: The country name derives from the ancient Greek word used to describe the inhabitants, aithiops , meaning "burnt appearance"

facts.title: Why it is called Finland
facts.body: Name derives from the Finns, an ethnic group in northeastern Europe; their name comes from the Germanic word finna , meaning "fish scale;" the local name, Suomi, may come from two local words: suo , meaning "marsh," and maa , meaning "land"

facts.title: Why it is called Fiji
facts.body: The Fijians called their home Viti, but the neighboring Tongans called it Fisi; in the Anglicized spelling of the Tongan pronunciation -- promulgated by explorer Captain James COOK -- the designation became Fiji

facts.title: Why it is called Micronesia
facts.body: The name is a 19th-century construct of two Greek words, mikros (small) and nesoi (islands), and refers to its thousands of small islands in the western Pacific Ocean

facts.title: Why it is called France
facts.body: Derives from the Latin name Francia, meaning "Land of the Franks"; the Franks were a group of Germanic tribes located along the middle and lower Rhine River in the 3rd century A.D.; the origin of the tribal name is unclear but may come from the Old German word franka , meaning "brave," or from a personal name such as Francio or Francus

facts.title: Why it is called Gabon
facts.body: Name originates from the Portuguese word gabão, meaning "cloak," possibly used by early explorers to describe the shape of the Komo River estuary

facts.title: Why it is called United Kingdom
facts.body: The name United Kingdom is self-descriptive; the name Britain probably derives from the Celtic word pretani , meaning "painted people;" the designation of Great Britain for England, Scotland, and Wales dates back to medieval times and was used to distinguish the island from Little Britain, or Brittany, in modern France; the name Ireland evolved from the Gaelic name Eriu, which is possibly derived from the Old Celtic iveriu , meaning "good land"

facts.title: Why it is called Grenada
facts.body: Origin of the name remains obscure; some sources attribute the designation to Spanish influence (most likely named for the Spanish city of Granada); in Spanish granada means "pomegranate"

facts.title: Why it is called Georgia
facts.body: The Western name probably derives from the name of the local people, the Gurz, whose name origin is uncertain; the native name "Sak'art'velo" means "Land of the Kartvelians" and refers to the core central Georgian region of Kartli

facts.title: Why it is called Ghana
facts.body: Named for a tribal chieftain who ruled a large part of the region prior to the 13th century, even though his territory was northwest of modern-day Ghana; the former name, Gold Coast, came from the gold that Portuguese explorers discovered in the region in the late 15th century

facts.title: Why it is called Gambia
facts.body: Named for the Gambia River that flows through the country; Portuguese explorers in the 15th century derived the name for the river from its local name, Ba-Dimma, meaning "the river"

facts.title: Why it is called Guinea
facts.body: The country is named after the Guinea region of West Africa that lies along the Gulf of Guinea, but the name itself derives from the Tuareg word aginaw , meaning "black people"

facts.title: Why it is called Equatorial Guinea
facts.body: The country is named for the Guinea region of West Africa that lies along the Gulf of Guinea and stretches north to the Sahel; the "equatorial" refers to the fact that the country lies just north of the Equator

facts.title: Why it is called Greece
facts.body: The English name derives from the Roman (Latin) designation Graecia , meaning "Land of the Greeks"; the Greeks call their country Ellas or Ellada, which is probably derived from Hellas, the name of the mythical son of Deucalian

facts.title: Why it is called Guatemala
facts.body: The Spanish conquistadors' first capital (established in 1524) was a former Mayan settlement called "Quauhtemallan" by their Nahuatl-speaking Mexican allies, a name that means "land of the eagle" but that the Spanish probably pronounced "Guatemala"

facts.title: Why it is called Guinea-Bissau
facts.body: The country is partly named after the Guinea region of West Africa that lies along the Gulf of Guinea; the name itself is derived from the Tuareg word aginaw , meaning "black people;" Bissau, the name of the capital city, distinguishes the country from neighboring Guinea and is derived from the local Bijuga people

facts.title: Why it is called Guyana
facts.body: The name is derived from Guiana, the original name for the region that included British Guiana, Dutch Guiana, and French Guiana; the name Guiana may be derived from a local term meaning "Land of Water" (referring to the area's multitude of rivers and streams)

facts.title: Why it is called Honduras
facts.body: The name means "depths" in Spanish and refers to the deep anchorage in the northern Bay of Trujillo

facts.title: Why it is called Croatia
facts.body: Name probably derives from the Croats, a Slavic tribe who migrated to the Balkans in the 7th century A.D., but that name may be related to the Russian word khrebet , meaning "mountain chain"

facts.title: Why it is called Haiti
facts.body: Derived from the Arawak name Ayti, meaning "Land of Mountains," that was originally applied to the entire island of Hispaniola

facts.title: Why it is called Hungary
facts.body: The Byzantine Greeks referred to the tribes that arrived on the steppes of Eastern Europe in the 9th century as the "Oungroi," a name that later became "Hungari," which originally meant an "[alliance of] ten tribes;" the Hungarian name Magyarorszag means "Country of the Magyars," which may be derived from the name of the most prominent of the Hungarian tribes

facts.title: Why it is called Indonesia
facts.body: The name is an 18th-century construct of two Greek words, "Indos" (India) and "nesoi" (islands), meaning "Indian islands"

facts.title: Why it is called Ireland
facts.body: The Irish name Eire evolved from the Gaelic name Eriu, which is possibly derived from the Old Celtic iveriu , meaning "good land;" the English name, Ireland, is a direct translation

facts.title: Why it is called Israel
facts.body: Named after the ancient Kingdom of Israel; according to Biblical tradition, the Jewish patriarch Jacob received the name Israel (meaning "He who struggles with God") after he wrestled with an angel of the Lord

facts.title: Why it is called India
facts.body: The English name derives from the Indus River; the Indian name, Bharat, may derive from the Bharatas tribe mentioned in the Sanskrit Vedas (Hindu religious texts); the name is also associated with Emperor Bharata, the legendary conqueror of India

facts.title: Why it is called Iraq
facts.body: The name probably derives from Uruk ("Erech" in Aramaic), the ancient Sumerian and Babylonian city on the Euphrates River

facts.title: Why it is called Iran
facts.body: The name derives from the Sanskrit word arya , referring to people living in a mountainous land, from the root word ar -, or "mountain;" the former name, Persia, was originally "Pars" (or the Arabic-influenced variant "Fars") from the Old Persian parsi , meaning "pure"

facts.title: Why it is called Iceland
facts.body: Floki VILGERDARSON, an early Norse explorer of the island in the 10th century, applied the name "Land of Ice," from the local words ís (ice) and land (land)

facts.title: Why it is called Italy
facts.body: Derivation is unclear; traditionally said to come from the Vitali, a tribe that settled in what is now Calabria, and whose name is believed to be linked to the Latin word vitulus , or "calf;" alternatively, the name may derive from a local ruler known to the Romans as Italus

facts.title: Why it is called Jamaica
facts.body: From the Arawak word xaymaca , meaning "Land of Wood and Water" or possibly "Land of Springs"

facts.title: Why it is called Jordan
facts.body: Named for the Jordan River, which makes up part of Jordan's northwest border; the origin of the river's name is unclear, but it may come from a local word meaning "river"

facts.title: Why it is called Japan
facts.body: The English word for Japan comes from the Chinese name for the country, Cipangu; both Nihon and Nippon come from the Japanese words nichi , or "sun," and hon , or "origin," which is frequently translated as "Land of the Rising Sun"

facts.title: Why it is called Kenya
facts.body: Named for Mount Kenya; the mountain's name may derive from the Kikuyu word kere nyaga , or "white mountain"

facts.title: Why it is called Kyrgyzstan
facts.body: Named for the local Kyrgyz people, with "-stan" coming from the Persian word ostan , meaning "country;" the Kyrgyz name may derive from the Turkic root words kir , or "steppe," and gismek , "to wander;" the name is traditionally said to come from a combination of the Turkic words kyrg (forty) and - is (hundred), based on a tale about two tribes and the number of their tents

facts.title: Why it is called Cambodia
facts.body: The name is derived from Kambu, a legendary ancestor of the Cambodian people

facts.title: Why it is called Kiribati
facts.body: The name is the local pronunciation of "Gilbert," the former designation of the islands; originally named after explorer Thomas GILBERT, who mapped many of the islands in 1788

facts.title: Why it is called Comoros
facts.body: Name derives from the Arabic al qamar , meaning "the moon"

facts.title: Why it is called Saint Kitts and Nevis
facts.body: Explorer Christopher COLUMBUS visited the islands in 1493 and named one for his own patron saint; a common nickname for Christopher during the following centuries was Kit or Kitt, and Saint Kitts is still referred to as Saint Christopher; the name of Nevis is said to derive from the original Spanish name "Las Nieves" (The Snows) and refers to its cloud-topped mountain

facts.title: Why it is called North Korea
facts.body: Derived from the Chinese name for Goryeo, which was the Korean dynasty that united the peninsula in the 10th century A.D.; the North Korean name "Choson" means "[Land of the] Morning Calm"

facts.title: Why it is called South Korea
facts.body: Derived from the Chinese name for Goryeo, which was the Korean dynasty that united the peninsula in the 10th century A.D.; the South Korean name "Han'guk" derives from the long form, "Taehan-min'guk," which is itself a derivation from "Daehan-je'guk," which means "the Great Han Empire"

facts.title: Why it is called Kuwait
facts.body: The name derives from the capital city, which comes from the Arabic al-kuwayt , itself a diminutive of the Hindustani term kut , meaning a fortress-like house

facts.title: Why it is called Kazakhstan
facts.body: The name may derive from the Turkic word kazak, meaning "nomad;" the Persian suffix - stan means "place of" or "country"

facts.title: Why it is called Laos
facts.body: Name means "Land of the Lao [people];" it derives from the name of the country's founder, Lao

facts.title: Why it is called Lebanon
facts.body: Derives from the Semitic root lbn, meaning "white," and probably refers to the country's snow-capped mountains

facts.title: Why it is called Saint Lucia
facts.body: Believed to be named after Saint LUCY (Sainte ALOUSIE) of Syracuse by French sailors who were shipwrecked on the island on 13 December 1502, the saint's feast day

facts.title: Why it is called Liechtenstein
facts.body: Named after the Liechtenstein family that purchased and united the counties of Schellenburg and Vaduz in 1719; the family name was taken from its Austrian castle of the same name, which in German means "light stone"

facts.title: Why it is called Sri Lanka
facts.body: The name is composed of the Sanskrit words shri (happiness or holiness) and lanka (island); the former name Serendib was an Arabic derivation of the Sanskrit word simhaladvipa , or "island of the place of lions;" the former name Ceylon came from the Sanskrit simha , or "lion"

facts.title: Why it is called Liberia
facts.body: Name derives from the Latin word liber, meaning "free;" so named because the nation was created as a homeland for liberated African-American slaves

facts.title: Why it is called Lesotho
facts.body: The name comes from the Sotho people, whose name means "dark-skinned;" Le - is a singular noun prefix; the former name, Basutoland, uses the plural noun prefix, Ba -

facts.title: Why it is called Lithuania
facts.body: Meaning of the name is obscure; may be derived from the local words lietava , meaning "small river," or lietus , meaning "rain" or "land of rain," or the Latin word litus , meaning "shore"

facts.title: Why it is called Luxembourg
facts.body: Probably derived from an early Celtic or Germanic form of the name, Lucilinburhuc, that was thought to mean "little fortress;" the name first referred to the city and was later used for the country

facts.title: Why it is called Latvia
facts.body: The name originates from the Latgalians, one of four eastern Baltic tribes that formed the ethnic core of the Latvian people (ca. 8th-12th centuries A.D.)

facts.title: Why it is called Libya
facts.body: The name probably derives from the Libu, a North African tribe first mentioned in texts from the 13th century B.C.; the ancient Greeks and Romans used the name for the entire North African coast west of Egypt

facts.title: Why it is called Morocco
facts.body: The English name of Morocco derives from, respectively, the Spanish and Portuguese names Marruecos and Marrocos, which stem from Marrakesh, the Latin name for the former capital of ancient Morocco; the Arabic name, Al Maghrib, translates as "The West"

facts.title: Why it is called Monaco
facts.body: Founded as a Greek colony in the 6th century B.C., the name's origin is unclear; it could derive from the Greek term monoikos (solitary), the Ligurian word monegu (rock), or the Basque word muno (mountain)

facts.title: Why it is called Moldova
facts.body: Named for the Moldova River in neighboring eastern Romania; the river's name probably comes from the Indoeuropean root word mel , meaning "dark" or "black"

facts.title: Why it is called Montenegro
facts.body: The name in Italian means "dark mountain" and is a translation of the Serbo-Croatian name Crna Gora; both refer to the dark coniferous forests in the mountainous region

facts.title: Why it is called Madagascar
facts.body: A variant of the name was first used by 13th-century Venetian explorer Marco POLO when he confused the island with the Somali port of Mogadishu; the transliteration was later adopted as the official name

facts.title: Why it is called Marshall Islands
facts.body: Named after British Captain John MARSHALL, who charted many of the islands in 1788

facts.title: Why it is called North Macedonia
facts.body: The name derives from the ancient kingdom of Macedon (7th to 2nd centuries B.C.), whose name origin is unclear; it may derive from the mythological Macedon, the son of the Greek god Zeus; alternatively, it may come from the Greek word makednos , meaning "tail," or the Illyrian word maketia , meaning "cattle"

facts.title: Why it is called Mali
facts.body: Name derives from the Mali Empire of the 13th to 16th centuries A.D.; the Mali name may come from a local ethnic group, the Malinke, whose name is derived from the words ma , meaning "mother," and dink , meaning "child" -- a reference to the matrilinear descent of Malinke families

facts.title: Why it is called Myanmar
facts.body: Both "Burma" and "Myanmar" derive from the name of the majority Burman (Bamar) ethnic group, with the term myanma , or "the strong," being the group's name for itself

facts.title: Why it is called Mongolia
facts.body: Name comes from the Mongol people, whose name derives from the Mongol root word mengu or mongu , meaning "brave" or "unconquered;" the Mongolian name Mongol Uls translates as "Mongol State"

facts.title: Why it is called Mauritania
facts.body: Named for the ancient kingdom of Mauretania (3rd century B.C. to 1st century A.D.); its name derives from the Mauri (Moors) of northwest Africa

facts.title: Why it is called Malta
facts.body: The origin is unclear; the name may come from the ancient term mel , meaning "high" and probably referring to the island's rocks; the ancient Greeks called the island "Melite," possibly from the Greek word meli, meaning "honey" and referring to the island's honey production

facts.title: Why it is called Mauritius
facts.body: Named after Prince Maurice VAN NASSAU, stadtholder (governor) of the Dutch Republic, in 1598

facts.title: Why it is called Maldives
facts.body: The origin of the name is obscure but may derive from the Sanskrit word maladvipa , meaning "garland of islands;" the local name, Dhivehi Raajje, means "land of the Dhivehi people" in the local language

facts.title: Why it is called Malawi
facts.body: Named for the Maravi people who inhabited the area since the 14th century; the word maravi means "flames"

facts.title: Why it is called Mexico
facts.body: Name may derive from one of the Nahuatl (Aztec) names for the capital city, Metztlixihtlico, which probably meant "the center of the moon;" alternatively, it may come from Mexica, the original name of the Aztec people

facts.title: Why it is called Malaysia
facts.body: Devised in the early 19th century by British geographers; the suffix - sia was added to the name of the Malay people to form a classical-style name; the name Malay may come from the Tamil word malai , meaning "mountain"

facts.title: Why it is called Mozambique
facts.body: Named for an offshore island; the island was named after Mussa bin BIQUE (or Mussa Ibn MALIK), an influential Arab slave trader who set himself up as sultan on the island in the 15th century

facts.title: Why it is called Namibia
facts.body: Named for the coastal Namib Desert; the word namib comes from the local Nama language and means "an area where there is nothing"

facts.title: Why it is called Niger
facts.body: Named for the Niger River that passes through the southwest of the country; the name of the river probably comes from the local Tuareg name, egereou n-igereouen (big rivers)

facts.title: Why it is called Nigeria
facts.body: Named for the Niger River that flows through the west of the country to the Atlantic Ocean; the name of the river probably comes from the local Tuareg name, egereou n-igereouen (big rivers)

facts.title: Why it is called Nicaragua
facts.body: 16th-century Spanish explorer Gil GONZALEZ Davila is said to have combined the name of a local chieftain, Nicarao, with the Spanish word agua (water), referring to the two large lakes in the west of the country (Lake Managua and Lake Nicaragua)

facts.title: Why it is called Netherlands
facts.body: The English name is derived from the country's Dutch name, which means "the lowlands" and describes the geographic area; only about half the Netherlands is more than 1 meter (3.3 ft) above sea level

facts.title: Why it is called Norway
facts.body: Derives from the Old Norse words norre and vegr , meaning "northern way," and refers to the long coastline of western Norway

facts.title: Why it is called Nepal
facts.body: The name probably comes from the Sanskrit term nepala , from the words for "fly down" and "house," which would refer to the villages at the base of the mountains

facts.title: Why it is called Nauru
facts.body: The island name may derive from the Nauruan word "anaoero" meaning "I go to the beach"; the former name, Pleasant Island, came from British navigator John Frean, who visited in 1798

facts.title: Why it is called New Zealand
facts.body: The name is an anglicized form of the Dutch name Nieuw Zeeland, or "New Sea Land," which was first used in 1643 in honor of the Dutch province of Zeeland

facts.title: Why it is called Oman
facts.body: The origin of the name is uncertain, but it may date back at least 2,000 years, with an "Omana" mentioned by Pliny the Elder (1st century A.D.) and an "Omanon" by Ptolemy (2nd century A.D.); it is said to derive from Oman ben Ibrahim al Khalil (Oman ben Kahtan), who founded the state

facts.title: Why it is called Panama
facts.body: Origin is unclear; may come from a Guarani word meaning "place of many fish"

facts.title: Why it is called Peru
facts.body: The name may derive from the Guarani word biru, meaning "river"

facts.title: Why it is called Papua New Guinea
facts.body: The name derives from the Malay word pua-pua , describing the tightly curled hair of the Papuan people; Spanish explorer Ynigo ORTIZ de RETEZ applied the term "Nueva Guinea" to the island in 1545 because he thought the locals resembled the peoples of the Guinea coast of Africa

facts.title: Why it is called Philippines
facts.body: Named in honor of King PHILLIP II of Spain by Spanish explorer Ruy LOPEZ de VILLALOBOS, who visited the islands in 1543

facts.title: Why it is called Pakistan
facts.body: The name is said to have been proposed in the early 1930s by Muslim students at Cambridge University, created from the initials of Punjab, Afghanistan, and Kashmir; the word pak also means "pure" in Persian or Pashto, and the Persian suffix - stan means "place of" or "country," so Pakistan literally means "Land of the Pure"

facts.title: Why it is called Poland
facts.body: The name probably comes from the Slavic word pole ( field or plain), indicating the flat nature of the country

facts.title: Why it is called Palestine
facts.body: Name refers to the location of the British Mandate of Palestine that was occupied and administered by Jordan in 1948, on the west bank of the Jordan River; the designation was retained after the 1967 Six-Day War and subsequent changes in administration

facts.title: Why it is called Portugal
facts.body: Name derives from the Roman designation "Portus Cale," meaning "Port of Cale;" Cale was located in present-day northern Portugal, and its name is said to come from the Latin word calere (to be warm) because the harbor never iced over

facts.title: Why it is called Palau
facts.body: From the Palauan name for the islands, Belau, which likely derives from the Palauan word beluu , meaning "village"

facts.title: Why it is called Paraguay
facts.body: Derives from the river of the same name; the river's name may come from the Guarani words para (water or river) and guay (born)

facts.title: Why it is called Qatar
facts.body: The name may derive from the Arabic word katran , meaning "tar" or "resin" in reference to the area's oil and natural gas reserves

facts.title: Why it is called Romania
facts.body: The name derives from the Latin Romani , meaning "people from Rome;" the area was an outpost of the Roman Empire in the 2nd century A.D., and the current name was adopted when Moldavia and Wallachia merged in 1861

facts.title: Why it is called Serbia
facts.body: The country takes its name from the Serb people; the origin of their name is unclear but may derive from the Caucasian root word ser , meaning "man"

facts.title: Why it is called Russia
facts.body: Russian lands were referred to as Muscovy until PETER I declared the Empire of All Russias in 1721; the new name aimed at identifying the new Russia with European political tradition; "Rus" was the Old Finnish name given to Varangians (eastern Vikings) who entered the area in the 9th century

facts.title: Why it is called Rwanda
facts.body: The country is named for a local people, but the meaning of their own name is obscure

facts.title: Why it is called Saudi Arabia
facts.body: Named after the ruling dynasty of the country, the House of Saud; the name Arabia can be traced back at least as far as the ancient Romans, who referred to the peninsula as "Arabia Felix" (Arabia the Fortunate)

facts.title: Why it is called Solomon Islands
facts.body: Spanish explorer Alvaro de MENDANA named the isles in 1568 after the wealthy biblical King SOLOMON in the mistaken belief that the islands contained great riches

facts.title: Why it is called Seychelles
facts.body: Named by French Captain Corneille Nicholas MORPHEY after Jean Moreau de SÉCHELLES, the finance minister of France, in 1756; the British changed the spelling of the name in 1815 when they acquired the islands

facts.title: Why it is called Sudan
facts.body: The name derives from the Arabic balad-as-sudan , meaning "Land of the Black [peoples]"

facts.title: Why it is called Sweden
facts.body: Name derives from the North Germanic Svea tribe that inhabited central Sweden; the tribe's name probably comes from the Old German word sweba , meaning "independent;" the local form of the country's name, Sverige, means "kingdom of the Svea"

facts.title: Why it is called Singapore
facts.body: Name derives from the Sanskrit words simha (lion) and pur (city); according to Malayan folklore, an Indian prince visited Singapore in the 7th century and mistook the first animal he saw for a lion, which is not native to the country

facts.title: Why it is called Slovenia
facts.body: The country's name means "Land of the Slavs" in Slovene; the origin of the Slav name is unclear, although early forms were used in Medieval Latin (Sclavus) and Byzantine Greek (Sklabos)

facts.title: Why it is called Slovakia
facts.body: The country takes its name from the local Slav ethnic group; the origin of the group's name is unclear, although early forms were used in Medieval Latin (Sclavus) and Byzantine Greek (Sklabos)

facts.title: Why it is called Sierra Leone
facts.body: Portuguese explorer Pedro de SINTRA is usually credited with naming the country "Serra da Leao" (Lion Mountains) in 1462, but Venetian explorer Alvise CA' DA MOSTO recorded the name as "Serre-Lionne" in 1457, referring to the rumbling of thunder over the mountains

facts.title: Why it is called San Marino
facts.body: Named after Saint MARINUS, who founded a monastic settlement on Monte Titano in the early 4th century

facts.title: Why it is called Senegal
facts.body: Named for the Senegal River that forms the northern border of the country; the river's name may derive from "Azenegue," the Portuguese name for the Berber Zenaga people who lived north of the river, or it could come from a local word meaning "navigable"

facts.title: Why it is called Somalia
facts.body: The name means "Land of the Somali," a local ethnic group; the origin of the group's name is unclear but may come from 1) a Cushitic word meaning "dark," 2) the local phrase soo mal , meaning "go and milk" (referring to offering guests milk), 3) the name of a local chief, or 4) the Arabic zamla , meaning "cattle"

facts.title: Why it is called Suriname
facts.body: Name may derive from the Surinen people who inhabited the area at the time of European contact

facts.title: Why it is called South Sudan
facts.body: Self-descriptive name from the country's geographic position within Sudan prior to independence; the name Sudan derives from the Arabic balad-as-sudan , meaning "Land of the Black [peoples]"

facts.title: Why it is called São Tomé and Príncipe
facts.body: Sao Tome was named after Saint THOMAS the Apostle by the Portuguese who discovered the island on 21 December 1470 (or 1471), the saint's feast day; Principe is a shortening of the original Portuguese name of "Ilha do Principe" (Isle of the Prince), referring to Prince ALPHONSO of Portugal

facts.title: Why it is called El Salvador
facts.body: Means "the Savior" in Spanish and is a shortened form of "the Divine Savior of the World" (el Divino Salvador del Mundo), referring to Jesus Christ; 16th-century Spanish colonists gave the name "San Salvador" to the fort located where the country's capital of San Salvador now stands, and the name was later used for the city and the surrounding region; the country was officially named El Salvador in 1824

facts.title: Why it is called Syria
facts.body: The source of the name is uncertain; the name appears as "Suri" in Babylonian cuneiform writings dating from about 4000 B.C.

facts.title: Why it is called Eswatini
facts.body: The country name derives from 19th century King MSWATI II, under whose rule Swati territory was expanded and unified

facts.title: Why it is called Chad
facts.body: Named for Lake Chad, which lies along the country's western border; taken from a local word meaning "large body of water" or "lake"

facts.title: Why it is called Togo
facts.body: The name derives from the town of Togodo (now Togoville) on the northern shore of Lake Togo; the town's name probably comes from the lake's name, which is composed of the Ewe words to ("water") and go ("shore")

facts.title: Why it is called Thailand
facts.body: The name means "Land of the Thai," referring to the local population; the people's name comes from the Thai word tha , meaning "to be free;" the former name of Siam comes from the Sanskrit word syama , meaning "dark"

facts.title: Why it is called Tajikistan
facts.body: The Persian suffix - ostan means "land," so the country name means "Land of the Tajik [people];" the name Tajik comes from the Sanskrit tajika , a name originally used to distinguish Arabs from Turks and derived from the Tay, an Arab people

facts.title: Why it is called Timor-Leste
facts.body: The name partly derives from the Indonesian and Malay word timur , meaning "east;" leste is the Portuguese word for "east," so "Timor-Leste" literally means "Eastern-East"

facts.title: Why it is called Turkmenistan
facts.body: The suffix - stan means "land," so the country name means the "Land of the Turkmen [people];" the people's name means "Turk-like," from the Persian words tork and mandan , referring to their formerly nomadic lifestyle that differed from the settled Turks of Turkey

facts.title: Why it is called Tunisia
facts.body: The country name derives from the capital city of Tunis

facts.title: Why it is called Tonga
facts.body: The name is of local origin and is said to mean "island;" the former name, the Friendly Islands, came from Captain James COOK in 1773, based on the welcome he received from the inhabitants

facts.title: Why it is called Trinidad and Tobago
facts.body: Explorer Christopher COLUMBUS named the larger island "La Isla de la Trinidad" (The Island of the Trinity) in 1498, possibly because of the three mountain peaks on the island; COLUMBUS may have gotten the name Tobago, spelled "tobaco" in Spanish, from the tobacco grown and smoked locally, or from its elongated cigar shape

facts.title: Why it is called Tuvalu
facts.body: The name in the local language means "group of eight" or "eight standing together," referring to eight of the country's nine islands; the remaining island, Nui, was left out of the original grouping because its inhabitants spoke a different language; the former name was given in honor of Canadian shipping company owner Alexander Ellice, who owned a ship that visited the islands in 1819

facts.title: Why it is called Tanzania
facts.body: The country's name is a combination of the first letters of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, the two states that merged to form Tanzania in 1964

facts.title: Why it is called Ukraine
